definition_zh: 提及；说起；提到的话；嘉奖；更不用说
definition_en: to speak or write about something briefly; also a short reference, a formal naming for praise, or a phrase that adds a stronger point
core_image: 一个人说话时顺手把某件事轻轻带过，只用半句话点到
scene: 会议开到一半，有人问起预算，负责人只在纸上写了一行小字。At the meeting she mentioned the budget only once, then moved on.
sceneCN: 这里是「提到、说起」（第 1 个义项：口头或书面简短提及）；句意为她在会上只提了一次预算，随后就继续往下说。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、纸笔、写着一行小字的便笺。

pos.zh: 提到；说起；点名表扬
提及；提到

derivatives.zh: 由 mention 加 -able 构成，义为「值得一提的」
由 un- 加 mentionable 构成，义为「不宜提及的；说不出口的」
由 afore（在前面）与 mentioned 复合而成，义为「上述的」

senses.title: To refer to something briefly
senses.definition: to say or write something about someone or something, without going into detail
senses.definitionCN: 简短地说到或写到某人或某事，不作详细展开
senses.example: She mentioned your name at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上提到了你的名字。
senses.why: The Latin noun mentio is a calling to mind; to mention something is to bring it into the listener's mind for a moment, not to dwell on it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 mentio 本义是「唤起心中的记忆」；mention 一件事，就是把它在听者心里唤起来一小会儿，而不是停下来细讲。

senses.title: A brief reference
senses.definition: a short remark or written reference to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事的简短评论或书面提及
senses.example: There was no mention of the price in the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 信里没有提到价格。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act, the noun can name the act itself as a thing: a mention is the small trace the act leaves in speech or text.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然指「提到」这个动作，名词就可以把动作本身当成一件事来指：a mention 就是这一动作在话语或文字里留下的一点小痕迹。

senses.title: To name someone for praise
senses.definition: to name a person formally, especially in a military report, as deserving recognition
senses.definitionCN: 正式点出某人的名字以示表彰，尤指在军方报告中
senses.example: The officer was mentioned in dispatches for his conduct.
senses.exampleCN: 这名军官因表现突出在战报中受到嘉奖。
senses.why: A formal report lists names one by one; naming a person in that list is a kind of mention, so the word comes to mean official recognition.
senses.whyCN: 正式报告会逐个列出名字；把某人写进这份名单，本身就是一种 mention，于是这个词引申为官方表彰。

senses.title: An added point that strengthens the statement
senses.definition: used to introduce a further fact that makes what has just been said stronger
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出更进一步的事实，使刚说过的话更有分量
senses.example: He speaks three languages, not to mention his fluent Chinese.
senses.exampleCN: 他会说三种语言，更不用说他那口流利的中文了。
senses.why: The phrase not to mention began as a way of saying 'without even speaking of', and it turned a bare mention into a rhetorical upgrade.
senses.whyCN: 短语 not to mention 起初表示「连说都不用说」，于是把一个轻描淡写的提及变成了加强语气的修辞手段。

intro.en: Mention comes from a Latin noun for calling something to mind, and its history keeps the idea of the mind rather than the mouth.
intro.cn: mention 来自拉丁语中表示「把某事唤到心上」的名词，它的历史始终围绕「心」而不是「嘴」。

items.en: Mentio meant a mentioning or a calling to mind, and it was formed on the root of mens, the mind.
items.cn: mentio 意为「提及、唤到心上」，由表示「心」的 mens 词根构成。

items.en: Mens named the mind or the thinking faculty; the same root produced memini, I remember, and memor, mindful.
items.cn: mens 指心智或思考能力；同一词根还产生 memini（我记得）与 memor（记着的）。

items.en: Old French took the Latin noun as mention and used it for a spoken or written reference.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁名词写作 mention，用于口头或书面的提及。

items.en: Middle English used mention as both noun and verb, and the verb soon became the everyday way to point at a topic.
items.cn: 中古英语中 mention 既作名词也作动词，动词很快成为点出一个话题的日常说法。

items.en: Modern English fixed the phrase not to mention and the military sense of being mentioned in dispatches.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了 not to mention 这一说法，以及「在战报中受到嘉奖」的军事义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the Latin mind-root or merely resemble the spelling; the near-meaning group collects verbs for pointing at a topic.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁「心」词根或只是拼写相像的词；近义组收表示「点出话题」的动词。

entries.definition: A remark that gives an opinion; it shares the ending but comes from Latin commentum, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 发表意见的评论；它与 mention 只是词尾相像，词源来自拉丁语 commentum，并非同根。

entries.definition: Relating to the mind; built on the same Latin root mens.
entries.definitionCN: 与心智有关的；建立在同一拉丁词根 mens 上。

entries.definition: A trusted adviser; the word goes back to the Greek name Mentor, not to the Latin mind-root.
entries.definitionCN: 可信赖的顾问；源自希腊人名 Mentor，与拉丁「心」词根无关，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A very short period of time; from Latin momentum, a movement or instant, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间；来自拉丁语 momentum（运动、瞬间），词源不同，仅拼写相近。

entries.definition: To speak about someone or something briefly.
entries.definitionCN: 简短地谈到某人或某事。

entries.definition: To mention something as an example or support.
entries.definitionCN: 举例或引证时提到某事。

entries.definition: To refer to something indirectly rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 间接地提及某事，而不直接点明。

entries.definition: To remark on something in speech or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 在口头或书面中谈到某事。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for memory and a root for mind; its family keeps speaking tied to thinking.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示记忆的拉丁名词与表示心智的词根上，同族词始终把「说」和「想」系在一起。

normal.en: Mentio in Latin is a calling to mind, so a mention brings a topic into the listener's head rather than into the centre of the talk.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mentio 是「唤到心上」，所以 mention 是把话题送进听者脑中，而不是摆到谈话中心。

normal.en: The root mens means mind, and mental still carries that meaning, which is why a mention is a mental event before it is a spoken one.
normal.cn: 词根 mens 意为心智，mental 至今保留此义，所以 mention 先是心里的事，然后才是嘴里的事。

normal.en: Mentioned in dispatches is a fixed military phrase: the name is written into a report, and writing a name is a literal mention.
normal.cn: mentioned in dispatches 是固定的军事说法：名字被写进报告，而写下一个名字就是字面意义上的 mention。

normal.en: Not to mention works like a hinge: it adds a stronger fact after a weaker one.
normal.cn: not to mention 像一扇铰链：先给一个较轻的事实，再挂上一个更重的。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling, so mention can be the act or the short reference it produces.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，所以 mention 既可以是「提到」这个动作，也可以是动作留下的那句短话。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tapping one word on a long page and then moving on; that tap is a mention.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在长页面上轻点一个词，然后继续移动；那一点就是 mention。

abstract.en: A mention is a small door: it lets a topic in without letting it take over the room.
abstract.cn: mention 是一扇小门：它让话题进来，却不让话题占满整个房间。

abstract.en: The word ties speech to memory, because what is mentioned is meant to stay in the mind afterwards.
abstract.cn: 这个词把说话和记忆系在一起，因为被提到的东西本来就是为了留在心里。

examples.en: She mentioned your name at the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会上提到了你的名字。

examples.en: There was no mention of the price in the letter.
examples.cn: 信里没有提到价格。

examples.en: He speaks three languages, not to mention his fluent Chinese.
examples.cn: 他会说三种语言，更不用说他那口流利的中文了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门神」——进门先看见门神，忍不住提一句；mention 意为提及。

root: 拉丁语 mentio（提及）来自 mens（心智）的词根 ment-；同族词多与「想、记、心」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a brief bringing-to-mind; it splits into the spoken reference, the formal naming for praise, and the phrase that adds a stronger point.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「把某事唤到心上的一提」；由此分出那句简短的提及、为表彰而点名的提及，以及用来加强语气的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tapping one word on a page and then moving on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指在页面上轻点一个词，随即移开。

branches.en: a speaker touching a topic and moving on
branches.cn: 说话人碰一下话题就继续往下

branches.en: a short line in a letter that keeps a topic alive
branches.cn: 信里短短一行字，让一个话题留在心上

branches.en: a name written into a military report
branches.cn: 名字被写进一份军方报告

branches.en: a hinge adding a heavier fact to a light one
branches.cn: 铰链一般，把更重的事实挂到轻的话后面

branches.en: the same small trace seen as act and as thing
branches.cn: 同一点小痕迹，既可以看作动作，也可以看作留下的东西

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin noun of memory, the root for mind, and two English suffixes that make it a quality or a possibility.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示记忆的拉丁名词、表示心智的词根，以及两个把它变成「性质」和「可能性」的英语后缀支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun mentio and the mind-root mens supply the core; English suffixes build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 mentio 与表示心智的词根 mens 提供核心，其余由英语后缀构成。

definition_zh: 商品；货物；（品牌或作品的）周边商品；推销、把……包装成商品；陈列商品以促进销售
definition_en: goods offered for sale, or the act of promoting goods by presenting them in an attractive or branded form
core_image: 货架上一排排贴着价签的货物，它们生来就是等着被换走的东西
scene: 货架上的帽子、杯子和海报都印着同一个名字，它们不是日用品，而是被专门摆出来卖的东西。The merchandise sells faster than the tickets themselves.
sceneCN: 商店入口处的架子上摆着帽子、杯子与海报，全都印着同一个名字，卖的是这个名号而不是实用品；句中的 merchandise 指「供出售的商品总称」（第 1 个义项：一切摆在货架上等待成交的货物）。图中可辨识物件：货架、帽子、杯子、海报、价签。

pos.zh: 商品；货物（总称）
（品牌或作品的）周边商品
推销；把……包装成商品；陈列商品

derivatives.zh: 商品促销；陈列设计
商品企划人员；促销陈列商
以商品形式推出的

senses.title: Goods offered for sale
senses.titleCN: 供出售的商品与货物总称
senses.definition: goods that are bought and sold, considered as a mass rather than one by one
senses.definitionCN: 被买卖的货物，按整体而不逐件看待
senses.example: The merchandise sells faster than the tickets themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 这些商品比门票本身卖得还快。
senses.why: the word descends from the Latin noun for wares, so it names goods as a category rather than a particular item.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自拉丁语中指「货物」的名词，因此它把货物当作一个类别，而非某一具体物件。

senses.title: Branded fan goods
senses.titleCN: 印有品牌或作品标识的周边商品
senses.definition: items carrying a brand, band or film name, sold as souvenirs or identity goods
senses.definitionCN: 印有品牌、乐队或影片名称，作为纪念品或身份象征出售的物品
senses.example: The band made more from merchandise than from the tour.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队靠周边商品赚的比巡演还多。
senses.why: when a name itself becomes the thing bought, the old word for goods narrows to branded goods.
senses.whyCN: 当被买走的是名号本身时，旧的「货物」一词就收窄为带品牌的商品。

senses.title: To promote as a product
senses.titleCN: 把某物包装成商品来推销
senses.definition: to present something as an attractive product in order to sell it
senses.definitionCN: 把某物呈现为有吸引力的产品以促成出售
senses.example: The studio merchandised the character across every format.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室把这个角色在各种载体上包装推销。
senses.why: the noun turned into a verb: to merchandise is to make a thing behave like goods on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：所谓推销，就是让一件东西表现得像货架上的商品。

senses.title: To arrange goods for sale
senses.titleCN: 通过陈列与展示促进销售
senses.definition: to display and present goods in a shop so that customers buy them
senses.definitionCN: 在店内陈列与布置商品，使顾客愿意购买
senses.example: She merchandised the window with autumn colours.
senses.exampleCN: 她用秋色调布置了橱窗。
senses.why: in retailing, the verb covers the whole craft of making goods look buyable, from shelf height to lighting.
senses.whyCN: 在零售业，这个动词涵盖让货看起来值得买的一整套手艺，从货架高度到灯光。

senses.title: Goods held as stock in accounts
senses.titleCN: 会计账上列为存货的商品
senses.definition: goods held for sale and recorded as a current asset in the accounts
senses.definitionCN: 为出售而持有、在账上记为流动资产的产品
senses.example: The audit found merchandise worth less than the book value.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现商品的实际价值低于账面价值。
senses.why: accounting needs a name for goods before they are sold, and it uses the trade word for them.
senses.whyCN: 会计需要为尚未售出的货物取名，于是用了这个行业词。

senses.title: Trade in physical goods
senses.titleCN: 以实物货物为对象的贸易（区别于服务贸易）
senses.definition: international trade in physical goods, as opposed to trade in services
senses.definitionCN: 以实物货物进行的国际贸易，以区别于服务贸易
senses.example: Merchandise trade fell while services trade held steady.
senses.exampleCN: 货物贸易下滑，服务贸易则保持平稳。
senses.why: statistics split trade into goods and services, and the older word for goods supplied the label for the first half.
senses.whyCN: 统计把贸易分为货物与服务两类，而指货物的旧词给了前一类名称。

senses.title: To trade, in older use
senses.definition: to buy and sell, or to trade in goods, in older English usage
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的英语中表示买卖或经营货物
senses.example: Merchants merchandised along the river in those years.
senses.exampleCN: 那些年商人们沿河做买卖。
senses.why: the verb once meant simply to carry on trade, before the modern sense of packaging goods for sale.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词一度只表示从事交易，后来才出现「把货包装成商品」的现代义。

senses.title: Anything packaged for selling
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：被包装成可售卖形式的内容或形象
senses.definition: any content, image or idea reshaped so that it can be sold like goods
senses.definitionCN: 任何被重新塑形、可以像货物一样出售的内容、形象或观念
senses.example: The documentary turned a private grief into merchandise.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片把私人的悲伤变成了可售卖的商品。
senses.why: the abstract sense strips away the shelf: what is sold is no longer an object but a packaged form.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义抽掉了货架：被卖的不再是实物，而是一种被包装过的形式。

intro.en: Merchandise comes through Old French marchandise from marchand 'merchant', which rests on Latin mercari 'to trade' and the noun merx 'wares'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: merchandise 经古法语 marchandise 来自 marchand「商人」，其根源是拉丁语 mercari「做买卖」与名词 merx「货物」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Merx (genitive mercis) meant 'wares, merchandise'. Its deeper origin is not established; the suggestions linking it to other Italic trading words or to Etruscan remain hypotheses.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。其更早来源未有定论；把它与其他意大利语族交易词或伊特鲁里亚语相联系的看法仍属假说。

items.en: Mercari 'to trade, deal in goods' is the verb built on merx, and its participle mercatus gave the Latin word for a market.
items.cn: mercari「做买卖、经营货物」是由 merx 构成的动词，其分词 mercatus 又给出拉丁语中「市场」一词。

items.en: Old French marchand 'merchant, trader' carried the Latin stock into French, and marchandise named what such a trader dealt in.
items.cn: 古法语 marchand「商人、交易者」把这一拉丁词干带入法语，marchandise 则指这种商人所经营的货。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the fourteenth century for goods bought and sold, and the verb followed soon after.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词指买卖的货物，动词义随后出现。

items.en: In the twentieth century merchandising came to mean the craft of presenting goods, and branded fan goods took the same name.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，商品陈列与促销成了一门手艺，带品牌的周边商品也用了同一个词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Latin etymon merx has no agreed pre-Latin origin, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：拉丁语词源 merx 没有公认的拉丁语之前来源，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same trading root; group two holds ordinary words for things that are sold.
note.cn: 第一组同出「交易」这一词根；第二组是表示可售之物的常用词。

entries.definition: A trader in goods, from the same French stem; it names the person where merchandise names the goods.
entries.definitionCN: 经营货物的商人，同出这一法语词干；它指人，而 merchandise 指货。

entries.definition: Relating to trade and merchants, built on the same stem with a Latin adjective suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 与贸易和商人有关的，由同一词干加拉丁形容词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Trade in general, built with the prefix for 'together' and the same root for wares.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指贸易，由表示「共同」的前缀与同一「货物」词根构成。

entries.definition: The place or system of buying and selling, from the Latin participle of the trading verb.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖的场所或体系，来自那个交易动词的拉丁分词。

entries.definition: The ordinary plural noun for things that are sold; merchandise is its commercial and formal counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指可售之物的普通复数名词；merchandise 是其商业、正式的说法。

entries.definition: An older word for articles offered for sale, still used in pottery and street trading.
entries.definitionCN: 指待售物品的较旧说法，仍用于陶器与街头买卖。

entries.definition: Goods kept in a shop or store; it stresses being held rather than being offered.
entries.definitionCN: 店铺或仓库中持有的货物；强调「存放」而非「待售」。

entries.definition: Anything made for sale, seen as the output of production rather than as goods on a shelf.
entries.definitionCN: 为出售而制造的任何东西，着眼点是生产产出而非货架上的货。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real merchant family, the real trade phrases and the real accounting use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的商人词族、真实的贸易搭配与真实的会计用法。

normal.en: The word and merchant share one stem: the merchant deals in merchandise.
normal.cn: 这个词与「商人」同出一个词干：商人经营的就是商品。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the trade: general merchandise, licensed merchandise, merchandise trade.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出行业义：日用百货、授权周边、货物贸易。

normal.en: The same stem gives commerce and market; all three circle buying and selling.
normal.cn: 同一词干还给出「商业」与「市场」，三者都围绕买卖。

normal.en: In shops, merchandising means how goods are displayed, not what they are.
normal.cn: 在店铺里，商品陈列讲的是货怎么摆，而不是货是什么。

normal.en: Accounting keeps merchandise for goods not yet sold; once sold, it becomes revenue.
normal.cn: 会计用这个词指尚未售出的货；一旦售出，它就变成收入。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf where every object wears the same name tag.
abstract.cn: 想象一个货架，每件东西都挂着同一个名字的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a memory being wrapped in paper and given a price.
abstract.cn: 想象一段回忆被包上纸、标上价格。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse where the boxes are ideas rather than objects.
abstract.cn: 想象一座仓库，箱子里装的不是物品而是观念。

examples.en: The shop ordered too much merchandise before the season changed.
examples.cn: 季节变化前，这家店订了太多商品。

examples.en: Merchandise trade between the two countries fell for a third year.
examples.cn: 两国之间的货物贸易连续第三年下滑。

examples.en: The museum merchandised its collection into posters, mugs and toys.
examples.cn: 博物馆把藏品做成了海报、杯子和玩具等商品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「merchant（商人）+ ise」——商人手里经营的东西 → 商品、货物

root: 古法语 marchandise（货物）来自 marchand（商人），再往上为拉丁语 mercari（做买卖）与 merx（货物）。merx 的更早来源无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow goods from the shelf outward: as stock, as a brand, as something to display, as an accounting entry, as a trade category and finally as anything packaged for sale.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让货物从货架向外走：它是存货、是品牌、是要陈列的东西、是账目上的一行、是贸易的一大类，最后成了任何被包装出售之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf of objects that all wait to be exchanged for money.
core.cn: 核心意象：一货架物品，全都等着被换成钱。

branches.en: PLAIN TRADING: goods and the act of trading them are the oldest layer of the word.
branches.cn: 朴素交易：货物与买卖货物这一动作，是这个词最古老的一层。

branches.en: THE NAME ITSELF: when a brand is what sells, goods become souvenirs of a name.
branches.cn: 名号本身：当卖的是品牌时，货物成了名号的纪念品。

branches.en: MAKING IT BUYABLE: the verb covers both packaging a thing and arranging it on a shelf.
branches.cn: 让它值得买：动词既指把东西包装成商品，也指把它摆上货架。

branches.en: COUNTING AND TRADE: accounts and statistics both need goods to be a measurable mass.
branches.cn: 记账与贸易：会计与统计都需要把货物当作可计量的一团。

branches.en: JUST THE PACKAGE: what remains is a form made sellable, with no object underneath.
branches.cn: 只剩包装：剩下的是一种被做成可售的形状，底下并没有实物。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root for wares plus a French noun ending, and the same root builds several everyday trading words.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「货物」词根加一个法语名词词尾，同一词根还构成了若干日常交易词。

latinIntro.en: Latin merx gives mercari, mercatus, commerce and merchant; the ending marks a noun of state or collection.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 merx 衍生出 mercari、mercatus、商业与商人等词；词尾标记状态或集合名词。

items.example: The root names goods as a mass.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把货物当作一团整体来命名。

items.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb describes the activity behind the goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述货物背后的活动。

items.example: The participle became the Latin word for a market.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了拉丁语中「市场」一词。

items.example: The French noun names the person in the trade.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词指从事交易的人。

items.example: The shelves were full of merchandise.
The merchant shipped cloth to three ports.
items.exampleCN: 这位商人把布运往三个港口。

items.example: Good merchandising lifts sales without a price cut.
items.exampleCN: 好的陈列能在不降价的情况下提升销量。

items.meaning: a person who plans product display
items.meaningCN: 负责商品企划与陈列的人
items.example: The merchandiser chose the shelf layout.
items.exampleCN: 商品企划人员选定了货架布局。

derivatives.zh: 商品促销；陈列设计
商品企划人员；促销陈列商
以商品形式推出的

definition_zh: 仁慈；怜悯；宽恕；宽大处理；幸事
definition_en: kindness shown to someone who could be punished or harmed, the act of forgiving, or a fortunate relief
core_image: 一只本可以落下的手，停在半空，改成了轻轻扶一把
scene: 法庭上，受害者家属沉默许久，最后没有要求最重的刑罚。The judge showed mercy and gave the young man a suspended sentence.
sceneCN: 这里是「仁慈、宽恕」（第 1 个义项：对有权惩罚的人手下留情）；句意为法官动了仁慈之心，判这个年轻人缓刑。图中可辨识物件：法庭木栏、卷宗、法官席。

pos.zh: 仁慈；怜悯；宽恕；宽大处理；幸事

derivatives.zh: 由 mercy 去 y 加 -ful 构成，义为「仁慈的；慈悲的」
由 mercy 去 y 加 -less 构成，义为「无情的；残忍的」
由 merciful 加 -ly 构成，义为「仁慈地；幸好」

senses.title: Compassion toward someone in your power
senses.definition: kindness and forgiveness shown to someone you have the power to punish or harm
senses.definitionCN: 对你本可以惩罚或伤害的人所表现的善意与宽容
senses.example: The judge showed mercy and reduced the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官动了仁慈之心，减轻了刑罚。
senses.why: The Latin word first meant a reward or a price paid; Christian writers used it for the unearned favour God gives, and that idea of a gift nobody earned became human compassion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词最初指「报酬、代价」；基督教作者用它表示上帝白白赐下的恩惠，而「不配得却得到的礼物」这一想法，后来变成了人对人的怜悯。

senses.title: Forgiveness instead of punishment
senses.definition: the act of forgiving an offender or treating them less severely than the rules allow
senses.definitionCN: 原谅犯错者，或对其处理得比规定更宽大
senses.example: She begged the court for mercy.
senses.exampleCN: 她向法庭求情，请求宽恕。
senses.why: Once mercy is a favour granted rather than earned, it naturally appears in courts, where the powerful can choose to relax the full weight of the law.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mercy 是不配得而得到的恩惠，它自然出现在法庭上——掌权者可以选择减轻法律的全力压迫。

senses.title: A fortunate relief
senses.definition: a welcome event that brings relief from pain or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 带来解脱、令人庆幸的事，使人脱离痛苦或困境
senses.example: It was a mercy that the fever broke before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 烧在黎明前退了，真是件幸事。
senses.why: If mercy is kindness that spares someone, an event that spares us suffering can be called a mercy too, as if the world had chosen to be kind.
senses.whyCN: 如果 mercy 是「手下留情」的善意，那么一件让我们免受痛苦的事也能叫 mercy，就好像这个世界选择对我们仁慈了一回。

senses.title: Completely in someone's power
senses.definition: used in the phrase at the mercy of, meaning completely controlled by another person or force
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 at the mercy of，意为完全受某人或某种力量支配
senses.example: The small boat was at the mercy of the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 小船只能任凭风摆布。
senses.why: To be at someone's mercy is to stand where their kindness or cruelty decides your fate, so the phrase pictures a person wholly handed over to another's will.
senses.whyCN: at someone's mercy 就是站在「对方的仁慈或残忍决定你命运」的位置上，这个短语画出一个人被完全交到别人意志里的样子。

intro.en: Mercy goes back to a Latin word for wages and price, and its move from payment to pardon is one of the most striking shifts in English.
intro.cn: mercy 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「报酬、代价」的词，它从「付钱」转向「宽恕」，是英语里最引人注目的词义变化之一。

items.en: Merces meant pay, wages or a price, the reward owed for work or for a service.
items.cn: merces 意为报酬、工资或代价，即为工作或服务应付的回报。

items.en: Christian writers used merces for the free favour and pardon given by God, a gift not earned by the receiver.
items.cn: 基督教作者用 merces 表示上帝白白赐予的恩惠与赦免，是接受者并未挣得的礼物。

items.en: Old French merci carried the sense of pity and mercy, and also served as a word of thanks.
items.cn: 古法语 merci 带有怜悯与仁慈的意思，同时也用作道谢之词。

items.en: Middle English mercy named both the virtue of compassion and the act of sparing an offender.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mercy 既指仁慈这种德性，也指饶恕犯错者的行为。

items.en: Modern English keeps the courtly and religious senses and adds the everyday phrase at the mercy of.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了法庭与宗教两方面的含义，又增添了日常短语 at the mercy of。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the Latin root for trade and reward; the near-meaning group gathers words for compassion and forgiveness.
note.cn: 形近组收来自拉丁语「交易、报酬」词根的词；近义组收表示怜悯与宽恕的词。

entries.definition: A soldier who fights for pay; from Latin mercenarius, from merces, wages.
entries.definitionCN: 为报酬而战的士兵；来自拉丁语 mercenarius，源出 merces（报酬）。

entries.definition: A person who buys and sells goods; from Latin mercari, to trade, from merx, merchandise.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖货物的人；来自拉丁语 mercari（做买卖），源出 merx（货物）。

entries.definition: Goods for sale; built on the Latin root merc-, trade.
entries.definitionCN: 待售的商品；建立在表示「交易」的拉丁词根 merc- 上。

entries.definition: Relating to trade and commerce; from the same Latin trading root.
entries.definitionCN: 与贸易、商业有关的；来自同一拉丁「交易」词根。

entries.definition: Sympathy for the suffering of others, with a wish to help.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人苦难的同情，并希望帮上一把。

entries.definition: A feeling of sorrow for someone's misfortune.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人不幸的难过之情。

entries.definition: The act of pardoning someone who has done wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 原谅犯错者的行为。

entries.definition: The quality of punishing less severely than allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 处罚比规定更宽大的做法。

normalIntro.en: The word moved from a price paid to a pardon given, and its family keeps the twin ideas of earning and giving.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「付出的代价」走向「给予的宽恕」，它的同族词则一直保留「挣得」与「给予」两条线索。

normal.en: Merces in Latin is wages or a price, so mercy begins in the world of payment and debt.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merces 是工资或代价，所以 mercy 最初属于「付钱与欠债」的世界。

normal.en: Christian Latin turned the word into God's free pardon, a gift the receiver could never earn.
normal.cn: 基督教拉丁语把这个词转为上帝白白的赦免，是接受者永远挣不到的礼物。

normal.en: Merchant and merchandise keep the trading sense of the same root, which is why they look and sound like mercy.
normal.cn: merchant 与 merchandise 保留同一词根的交易义，所以它们看起来、听起来都像 mercy。

normal.en: Merciful adds -ful to mercy, meaning full of mercy; merciless adds -less, meaning without it.
normal.cn: merciful 在 mercy 后加 -ful，意为「充满仁慈」；merciless 加 -less，意为「没有仁慈」。

normal.en: At the mercy of is a fixed phrase: the person stands exactly where another's kindness decides what happens.
normal.cn: at the mercy of 是固定短语：这个人就站在「别人的仁慈决定结果」的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand that stops halfway down and turns into a hand that lifts someone up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只已经抬起、准备落下的手，在半空停住，变成一只把人扶起的手。

abstract.en: Mercy is power that chooses not to spend itself.
abstract.cn: mercy 是选择不把力量全部用出去的力量。

abstract.en: A price and a pardon in one word reminds us that forgiving always costs someone something.
abstract.cn: 「代价」与「赦免」同处一词，提醒人：宽恕总要有人付出点什么。

examples.en: The judge showed mercy and reduced the sentence.
examples.cn: 法官动了仁慈之心，减轻了刑罚。

examples.en: She begged the court for mercy.
examples.cn: 她向法庭求情，请求宽恕。

examples.en: The small boat was at the mercy of the wind.
examples.cn: 小船只能任凭风摆布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没事」——本来要重罚，结果说没事；mercy 就是宽恕。

root: 拉丁语 merces（报酬、代价）经基督教拉丁语转为「上帝的恩惠」，再经古法语 merci（怜悯）进入英语；同族词多与交易、报酬有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is kindness that spares; it branches into courtroom forgiveness, fortunate relief, and the phrase for being wholly in another's power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「手下留情的善意」；由此分出法庭上的宽恕、令人庆幸的解脱，以及表示完全受制于人的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that could strike, held back and turned into a hand that lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只本可以打下去的手，收住了，变成一只扶人的手。

branches.en: a judgement seat where the heavier sentence is set aside
branches.cn: 审判席上，较重的刑罚被放到一边

branches.en: a court where the rules are deliberately softened
branches.cn: 法庭上有意把规矩放松一些

branches.en: a fever breaking before dawn
branches.cn: 烧在黎明前退了下去

branches.en: a small boat drifting where the wind sends it
branches.cn: 小船随风漂到哪里就是哪里

branches.en: the same spared outcome, given as feeling and as act
branches.cn: 同一种「免于受罚」的结果，一面是心软，一面是行为

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for pay and price, a Latin trading root, and two English suffixes for having and lacking a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词依托一个表示报酬与代价的拉丁名词、一个拉丁交易词根，以及两个表示「有」与「无」某种性质的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: A Latin noun of pay and a trading root stand behind the French word that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 一个表示报酬的拉丁名词与一个交易词根，支撑着英语借来的法语词形。

definition_zh: 仅仅的；只不过的；纯粹的；十足的；未掺杂的（古义）
definition_en: used to stress that something is no more than what is stated; also, in an older sense, pure and unmixed
core_image: 一杯没有兑水的酒，除此之外什么都没有
scene: 朋友兴冲冲地说起一个计划，其实那只是他昨晚随口想到的一句话。His plan was a mere guess, not a real study.
sceneCN: 这里是「仅仅的、只不过的」（第 1 个义项：强调某物不过如此）；句意为他那个计划只是一个猜测，并不是真正的研究。图中可辨识物件：写满字的草稿纸、咖啡杯。

pos.zh: 仅仅的；只不过的；纯粹的；十足的

derivatives.zh: 由 mere 加 -ly 构成，义为「仅仅；只不过」，常用于修饰动词或整句
由 mere 加 -ness 构成，义为「仅仅是某种东西的状态」，较少使用

senses.title: Nothing more than what is named
senses.definition: used before a noun to stress that the thing is small, simple, or unimportant, and no more than that
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，强调该事物很小、很简单或不重要，不过如此而已
senses.example: The damage was a mere scratch.
senses.exampleCN: 损坏只不过是一道划痕。
senses.why: The Latin source meant pure, with nothing mixed in; from 'nothing added' it was a short step to 'nothing more than', which is how the modern word is used.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词源义为「纯粹的、没有掺入别的」，从「没有添加」到「不过如此」，只差一小步，现代用法正是后者。

senses.title: Sheer and absolute
senses.definition: used to emphasize that a quality is complete and nothing else is involved
senses.definitionCN: 强调某种性质完完全全，别无其他成分
senses.example: We met by mere chance at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站相遇纯属偶然。
senses.why: If mere means unmixed, then mere chance is chance with nothing else behind it, and the word naturally strengthens the noun it modifies.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mere 有「未掺杂」之义，mere chance 就是背后别无其他的偶然，这个词自然会给它所修饰的名词加上分量。

senses.title: Pure and unmixed (archaic)
senses.definition: in older use, describing a substance that has nothing added to it
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的用法中，形容某物质没有掺入任何别的东西
senses.example: The old recipe called for mere wine, with no water added.
senses.exampleCN: 那份旧食谱要求用纯酒，不兑水。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense: a liquid that is itself alone, and the modern 'only' sense is the same idea moved from wine to ideas.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的物质义：一种只由自己构成的液体；现代的「只不过」义，就是把同一想法从酒搬到了观念上。

intro.en: Mere as 'only' and mere as 'lake' are two different words that happen to share a spelling; the adjective came from Latin by way of French.
intro.cn: 表示「只不过」的 mere 和表示「湖」的 mere 是两个碰巧同形的词；形容词这一支经法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: Merus meant pure and unmixed, and it was used of wine that had no water in it.
items.cn: merus 意为纯粹的、未掺杂的，常用来形容不兑水的酒。

items.en: The neuter noun merum named unmixed wine itself, a small but vivid trace of the original sense.
items.cn: 中性名词 merum 直接指未兑水的酒，是原义留下的一个小而生动的痕迹。

items.en: Old French mier or mer meant pure and simple, and English borrowed it in the sense of unmixed.
items.cn: 古法语 mier 或 mer 意为纯粹、单纯，英语借入时取「未掺杂」之义。

items.en: Middle English used mere for pure and unmixed things, then weakened it to mean nothing more than.
items.cn: 中古英语用 mere 形容纯粹、未掺杂之物，随后弱化为「不过如此」的意思。

items.en: The lake sense comes from Old English mere, a different word altogether, and it survives mainly in place names.
items.cn: 表示「湖」的义项来自古英语 mere，完全是另一个词，如今主要保留在地名里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely resemble the spelling; the near-meaning group collects words that also mean 'nothing more than'.
note.cn: 形近组收只是拼写相像的词；近义组收同样表示「不过如此」的词。

entries.definition: To combine into one; from Latin mergere, to dip, so only the spelling resembles mere.
entries.definitionCN: 合并为一体；来自拉丁语 mergere（浸入），只是拼写与 mere 相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: A quality that deserves praise; from Latin meritum, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 值得称赞的品质；来自拉丁语 meritum，词源不同，仅拼写相近。

entries.definition: Soft wet ground; from Old Norse, a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 松软的湿地；来自古诺尔斯语，词源不同。

entries.definition: Happy and lively; from Old English myrige, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 快乐活泼的；来自古英语 myrige，词源不同。

entries.definition: And no one or nothing else besides.
entries.definitionCN: 除此之外再没有别的。

entries.definition: Merely, with nothing more than that.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅，不过如此。

entries.definition: Complete and nothing else; used to stress a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 十足的、纯粹的；用来强调某种性质。

entries.definition: Complete and absolute, used of bad or surprising things.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的、绝对的，多用于糟糕或令人吃惊的事物。

normalIntro.en: The adjective began as a word for purity and ended as a word for 'nothing more'; a second, unrelated mere still means a lake.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词从「纯粹」出发，最后表示「不过如此」；另有一个毫无关系的 mere，仍然指「湖」。

normal.en: Merus in Latin means unmixed, so mere wine was wine with no water added.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merus 意为未掺杂的，所以 mere wine 就是不兑水的酒。

normal.en: The step from 'unmixed' to 'nothing more than' is easy: if nothing is added, then there is nothing else.
normal.cn: 从「未掺杂」走到「不过如此」并不难：既然没有添加，也就没有别的了。

normal.en: Merely is mere plus -ly, and it is the adverb you want when you mean 'only', not the adjective before a noun.
normal.cn: merely 是 mere 加 -ly，当你想说「仅仅」而修饰动词时用它，而不是用放在名词前的形容词。

normal.en: The lake mere comes from Old English and survives in names such as Windermere.
normal.cn: 表示「湖」的 mere 来自古英语，保留在 Windermere 这类地名里。

normal.en: Mere words is a common phrase because words alone, with no action, are exactly what mere means.
normal.cn: mere words 是常见搭配，因为只有话、没有行动，正是 mere 所表达的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of wine with nothing poured into it, then move that 'nothing added' idea onto a guess or a scratch.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯什么都没兑进去的酒，再把「没有添加」这个想法挪到一个猜测或一道划痕上。

abstract.en: Mere always shrinks the noun after it: the word itself is a small spotlight aimed at something small.
abstract.cn: mere 总是把它后面的名词缩小：这个词本身就是一盏照向小东西的小聚光灯。

abstract.en: One spelling for 'pure' and 'lake' shows how English lets two unrelated lives share a single coat.
abstract.cn: 「纯粹」与「湖」共用一个拼写，说明英语能让两个毫不相干的身世穿同一件外衣。

examples.en: The damage was a mere scratch.
examples.cn: 损坏只不过是一道划痕。

examples.en: We met by mere chance at the station.
examples.cn: 我们在车站相遇纯属偶然。

examples.en: The old recipe called for mere wine, with no water added.

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is 'nothing added'; it yields the everyday 'nothing more than', the emphatic 'sheer', and the archaic literal 'unmixed'.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「没有添加」；由此得到日常的「不过如此」、加强语气的「十足」，以及古老的字面义「未掺杂」。

core.cn: 核心意象：一杯没有兑入任何东西的酒，纯粹而孤立。

intro.en: The adjective rests on a Latin word for purity, its noun for unmixed wine, and an English adverb suffix that turns it into merely.
intro.cn: 这个形容词依托一个表示纯粹的拉丁词、一个指未兑水之酒的名词，以及一个把它变成 merely 的英语副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: A Latin adjective of purity and its noun for unmixed wine lead through French to the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 表示纯粹的拉丁形容词及其指未兑水之酒的名词，经法语通向英语形容词。

definition_zh: 仅仅；只不过；只是
definition_en: only, and nothing more than what is named

sceneCN: 这里指限定范围、排除更多要求（第 1 个义项：仅仅，别无其他）；句意为这份工作只需要耐心，并不需要特殊天赋；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 仅仅；只不过；只是

最微小的（最高级）

senses.title: Only and nothing more
senses.definition: used to limit a statement to what is named and exclude anything more
senses.definitionCN: 把陈述限定在所说的内容上，排除更多的东西
senses.example: He is merely a clerk in a large office.
senses.exampleCN: 他只是一家大事务所里的职员。
senses.why: The word draws a boundary around the description and denies any larger claim.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在描述周围画下一道边界，否认任何更大的说法。

senses.title: No more than
senses.definition: used to lower the importance of what follows
senses.definitionCN: 用来降低随后内容的重要性
senses.example: The delay was merely a technical glitch.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误不过是一个技术故障。
senses.why: Here the minimizer deflates significance, telling the listener not to treat the thing as serious.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个「缩小词」给重要性放气，告诉听者不必把此事看得严重。

senses.title: Only a matter of
senses.definition: used before a noun to reduce an issue to one simple factor
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，把问题归结为单一简单因素
senses.example: Success here is merely a question of timing.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里，成功只是时机问题。
senses.why: The pattern collapses a complex situation into one named factor, often for rhetorical effect.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式把复杂情形压缩成单一因素，常带修辞效果。

senses.title: Not merely
senses.definition: in the pattern not merely, used to say something is more than what is named
senses.definitionCN: 在「不只是」的结构中，表示某物超出所说的范围
senses.example: The law is not merely a set of rules but a social institution.
senses.exampleCN: 法律不只是一套规则，而是一种社会制度。
senses.why: Negating the minimizer opens the scale upward; the sentence promises a larger description to come.
senses.whyCN: 否定这个「缩小词」会把尺度向上打开，句子随即承诺一个更大的说法。

senses.title: Merely by doing
senses.definition: used to say that a small action is enough
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个小小的动作就已足够
senses.example: You can sharpen the image merely by changing one setting.
senses.exampleCN: 你只需改动一个设置就能让图像更清晰。
senses.why: The by-phrase presents the minimum sufficient means, with no extra effort implied.
senses.whyCN: 「通过」短语给出最小充分手段，暗示不需要额外努力。

senses.title: Merely because
senses.definition: used to say that a reason is the only one, often to criticize it as insufficient
senses.definitionCN: 表示这是唯一的理由，常含「理由不足」的批评
senses.example: They rejected the plan merely because it came from a newcomer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拒绝这个方案，仅仅因为它是新来的人提出的。
senses.why: The causal phrase usually carries disapproval: a single reason is treated as too thin.
senses.whyCN: 这一因果短语通常带不赞同：单一理由被视为过于单薄。

senses.title: Merely a formality
senses.definition: used of a step that must be done but has no real effect
senses.definitionCN: 指必须完成却没有实际作用的步骤
senses.example: The signature was merely a formality after the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 决定作出后，签字只是走个形式。
senses.why: The fixed phrase marks a procedure kept for appearance, not for function.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定短语指为了外观而保留的程序，而非为了功能。

senses.title: Downplaying in speech
senses.definition: used in conversation to soften a request or defend an intention
senses.definitionCN: 在对话中缓和请求或为自己的意图辩护
senses.example: I was merely asking, not accusing you.
senses.exampleCN: 我只是问问，并不是在指责你。
senses.why: In speech the word protects the speaker from a stronger reading of their act.
senses.whyCN: 在口语中，这个词保护说话者，免得自己的举动被读得过重。

intro.en: Merely comes from the Latin adjective for pure or unmixed, through French and English, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; the deeper origin of the Latin adjective is uncertain, and the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「纯粹的、未掺杂的」形容词，经法语与英语，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚；拉丁形容词的更早词根难以确证，英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The Latin adjective merus means pure, unmixed or nothing but.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词意为「纯粹的、未掺杂的」，引申为「不过是」。

items.en: Old French mier carries the sense of pure or entire into French.
items.cn: 古法语形容词把「纯粹、完整」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Middle English mere means pure or simple, and the modern sense of only develops from it.
items.cn: 中古英语形容词意为「纯粹的、简单的」，现代「仅仅」义由此发展。

items.en: The adverb merely grows out of the adjective with the usual suffix, first meaning purely and then only.
items.cn: 副词由形容词加常见后缀构成，先表「纯粹地」，再表「仅仅」。

items.en: The English adverb is recorded from the late medieval period; the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语副词见于中世纪末期，确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: The deeper root of the Latin adjective cannot be confirmed, and no confident Indo-European source can be named; this uncertainty concerns the root, not the clear Latin origin of the word itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词的更早词根难以确证，无法给出有把握的印欧语来源；这属于词根层面的存疑，而词本身的拉丁来源是清楚的。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin pure-root; the second group contrasts limits of scope with measures of small size.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「纯粹」词根；第二组对照「限定范围」与「衡量幅度小」。

entries.definition: Nothing more than; also, pure and unmixed in older use.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅、不过是；旧义也指纯粹、未掺杂的。

entries.definition: The superlative of mere, meaning the slightest or smallest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词的最高级，意为最微小的。

entries.definition: The quality of being pure or nothing but; rare.
entries.definitionCN: 纯粹或「仅是」的性质；少见。

entries.definition: Showy but cheap and false; it shares the letters mer- but not the pure-root.
entries.definitionCN: 华而不实、虚有其表的；只共享开头字母，并非同一词根。

entries.definition: No one or nothing else besides the one named.
entries.definitionCN: 除所说的人或物之外再无其他。

entries.definition: Simply, with no more than the named thing; also used for emphasis in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅，没有更多；口语中也用于加强语气。

entries.definition: In a plain way, without complication; sometimes close to merely.
entries.definitionCN: 以简单、不加复杂化的方式；有时接近「只不过」。

entries.definition: A phrase that explicitly denies any larger claim.
entries.definitionCN: 明示否认任何更大说法的短语。

entries.definition: Only just, in terms of quantity or degree, not scope.
entries.definitionCN: 就数量或程度而言「刚刚够」，不是限定范围。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pure-root, the real limiting patterns and the real speech use for softening.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「纯粹」词根、真实的限定句式，以及口语中缓和语气的真实用法。

normal.en: The root means pure or unmixed, so merely strips a statement down to one item.
normal.cn: 词根意为「纯粹、未掺杂」，所以这个词把一句话削到只剩一项。

normal.en: Not merely is the door that opens upward: there is always more to say.
normal.cn: 「不只是」是一扇向上的门：后面总有更多话要说。

normal.en: Merely by changing one setting shows how small the sufficient action can be.
normal.cn: 「只需改一个设置」说明充分行动可以多小。

normal.en: Merely because usually sounds like a complaint about a thin reason.
normal.cn: 「仅仅因为」听上去通常是在抱怨理由太薄。

normal.en: In an argument, merely asking is a shield, not a question.
normal.cn: 在争执中，「只是问问」是一面盾牌，而不是一个问题。

abstract.en: Limiting a thing to its name is a way of refusing to let it grow.
abstract.cn: 把事物限定在它的名称上，就是拒绝让它长大。

abstract.en: The word is small but it draws a hard line around a whole claim.
abstract.cn: 这个词很短，却在整段断言周围画出硬线。

abstract.en: Saying merely is often a way to be modest and firm at the same time.
abstract.cn: 说「仅仅」，常常是既谦逊又坚定。

examples.en: The change was merely cosmetic and fooled no one.
examples.cn: 这个改动只是表面功夫，骗不了任何人。

examples.en: She was not merely tired; she was ill.
examples.cn: 她不只是累了，而是病了。

examples.en: The fee is merely a formality to cover paperwork.
examples.cn: 这笔费用只是覆盖文书工作的形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「秘而利」——秘密很小，仅此而已

root: 拉丁语形容词「纯粹的、未掺杂的」经古法语与中古英语进入英语，先表「纯粹」，再发展出「仅仅」；副词由该形容词加后缀构成。直接拉丁来源清楚，但其更早词根难以确证，英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate bare limitation, lowered importance, a single-factor reduction, the not-merely expansion, minimum means, a thin reason, an empty formality and polite downplaying.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理纯粹的限定、降低重要性、归结为单一因素、「不只是」的扩展、最小手段、单薄理由、空洞形式，以及礼貌淡化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty box that contains only a slip reading nothing more.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只空盒子，里面只有一张写着「仅此而已」的纸条。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: the statement stops at what is named.
branches.cn: 边界：陈述停在所说的内容上。

branches.en: THE DEFLATION: lowering importance and reducing an issue to one factor.
branches.cn: 放气：降低重要性，把问题压成单一因素。

branches.en: THE OPEN SCALE: not merely promises something larger beyond the name.
branches.cn: 打开的尺度：「不只是」承诺名称之外还有更大内容。

branches.en: THE THIN SUFFICIENCY: the smallest means and the weakest reason.
branches.cn: 单薄的充分性：最小手段与最弱理由。

branches.en: THE EMPTY SHELL: a formality without effect and a polite shield in speech.
branches.cn: 空壳：无实效的形式与口语中的礼貌盾牌。

intro.en: Merely is a Latin pure-adjective, a French layer and an English adverb suffix; the deeper root of the Latin adjective is genuinely uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「纯粹」形容词、法语层与英语副词后缀构成；拉丁形容词的更早词根确实存疑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective for unmixed supplies the whole family, and its deeper origin cannot be traced with confidence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「未掺杂」形容词提供整个词族，其更早来源无法有把握地追溯。

items.example: The adjective describes wine with nothing added.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述没有掺入别物的酒。

items.example: The noun shows how concrete the image of purity first was.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词说明「纯」最初有多具体。

items.example: A related adjective keeps the same physical sense.
items.exampleCN: 一个相关形容词保留同样的具体含义。

items.example: French carries the sense forward before English borrows it.
items.exampleCN: 法语在英语借入前把这一含义传下去。

items.example: English shifts from purity to bare limitation.
items.exampleCN: 英语从「纯粹」转向「仅仅」这一限定义。

items.example: The superlative survives in phrases about the smallest trace.
items.exampleCN: 最高级仍保存在表示「最细微痕迹」的短语里。

items.example: The rare noun names the quality of being nothing more.
items.exampleCN: 这个少见名词命名「别无其他」的性质。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a limiter adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成限定副词。

items.example: The adverb is the form that limits a whole statement.
items.exampleCN: 副词形式用来限定整句陈述。

core_image: 太阳在天空升到最高，一条从南到北划过天顶的隐形大圆正好对着它
scene: 正午时分测量杆的影子缩到最短。At noon the sun crosses the meridian and the shadow reaches its shortest.
sceneCN: 这里 meridian 指「过南北两极、也过天顶的大圆」（第 7 个义项：观测者所在的天球子午圈）；句意为太阳经过这条大圆时正当正午，杆影最短。图中可辨识物件：测量杆、影子、太阳、南北方向的标线。

senses.title: A great circle through the poles
senses.titleCN: 子午线：过南北两极的大圆
senses.definition: a great circle on the earth passing through both poles and any given place
senses.definitionCN: 地球上过南北两极与某地的大圆
senses.example: Every place lies on its own meridian.
senses.exampleCN: 每个地方都位于自己的一条子午线上。
senses.why: Latin meridies meant 'midday'; the sun at noon lies on the north-south circle, so that circle became the meridian.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 meridies 意为「正午」；正午太阳位于南北向的圈上，这条圈因此被称为子午线。

senses.title: The prime meridian
senses.titleCN: 本初子午线：经度计数的零度线
senses.definition: the meridian chosen as zero longitude, internationally fixed at Greenwich
senses.definitionCN: 被选作零度经线的子午线，国际上定在格林尼治
senses.example: Longitude is counted east and west from the prime meridian.
senses.exampleCN: 经度从本初子午线向东、向西计数。
senses.why: One meridian must be chosen as the zero for all others, and that choice is a convention rather than a natural line.
senses.whyCN: 必须选一条子午线作为其它经线的零点，这个选择是约定而非天然界线。

senses.title: Midday or noon
senses.titleCN: 正午：太阳位于当地最高点的时间
senses.definition: the time of day when the sun is at its highest point, that is, local noon
senses.definitionCN: 太阳位于当地最高点的时间，即当地正午
senses.example: The ceremony took place at the meridian.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式在正午举行。
senses.why: Meridian comes straight from meridies 'midday', so the word can still name the hour itself, not only the line.
senses.whyCN: meridian 直接来自 meridies「正午」，因此这个词仍可指这个时刻本身，而不只是线。

senses.title: The sun's highest point
senses.titleCN: 太阳中天：太阳到达当日最高处的时刻
senses.definition: the moment when the sun reaches its greatest altitude and crosses the observer's meridian
senses.definitionCN: 太阳达到当日最大高度并经过观测者子午圈的时刻
senses.example: The astronomers recorded the meridian of the sun with a transit instrument.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家使用中星仪记录了太阳中天的时刻。
senses.why: The crossing of the meridian is the physical event that defines noon, so 'meridian' names both the line and the crossing.
senses.whyCN: 经过子午圈是定义正午的物理事件，因此 meridian 既指线也指这次经过。

senses.title: The peak of achievement
senses.titleCN: 顶点：事业或成就的最高处
senses.definition: the highest point of success, fame or a career
senses.definitionCN: 成功、名声或事业的最高点
senses.example: The composer was at his meridian when he wrote the symphony.
senses.exampleCN: 作曲家写这部交响曲时正处于创作顶峰。
senses.why: The sun at noon is at its highest, so the same word pictures any career at its high point.
senses.whyCN: 正午的太阳升到最高，同一个词便用来比喻任何事业的最高点。

senses.title: An acupuncture channel
senses.titleCN: 经络：中医里气血运行的通道
senses.definition: one of the channels in traditional Chinese medicine along which qi and blood are said to flow
senses.definitionCN: 中医认为气血运行的通道之一
senses.example: The acupuncturist traced a meridian down the patient's arm.
senses.exampleCN: 针灸师沿着病人手臂的一条经络施针。
senses.why: English translators needed a word for these channels and borrowed 'meridian', because a channel runs like a line across the body.
senses.whyCN: 英语译者需要为这些通道找词，便借用了 meridian，因为经络像一条线贯穿身体。

senses.title: The observer's celestial meridian
senses.titleCN: 天球子午圈：过天顶与天极的大圆
senses.definition: the great circle on the celestial sphere passing through the poles and the observer's zenith
senses.definitionCN: 天球上过天极与观测者天顶的大圆
senses.example: Stars rise and culminate on the celestial meridian.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星在天球子午圈上升起并达到中天。
senses.why: The zenith and the two celestial poles define one great circle, and observers track stars as they cross it.
senses.whyCN: 天顶与两个天极确定一条大圆，观测者就在恒星越过它时进行追踪。

senses.title: Meridian passage or transit
senses.titleCN: 中天：天体经过子午圈的时刻
senses.definition: the passage of a celestial body across the observer's meridian
senses.definitionCN: 天体经过观测者子午圈的时刻
senses.example: The planet's meridian was predicted for midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗行星的中天时刻被预测在午夜。
senses.why: Once the line is fixed, the event of crossing it needs a name too, so astronomy uses meridian for the transit.
senses.whyCN: 线固定之后，越过它的事件也需要名称，因此天文学用 meridian 指这次中天。

intro.en: Meridian comes from Latin meridianus 'of midday, southern', from meridies 'midday, south', itself from medius 'middle' and dies 'day'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: meridian 来自拉丁 meridianus「正午的、南方的」，源于 meridies「正午、南方」，而 meridies 由 medius「中间」与 dies「日」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Medius meant 'middle'; it marks the centre of the day, the point where the sun stands highest.
items.cn: medius 意为「中间的」；它标出一天的中心，也就是太阳最高之处。

items.en: Dies meant 'day'; its deeper origin is connected with a root for brightness, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: dies 意为「日、白天」；其更深来源与表示明亮的词根相关，属重构形式而非有记录的词。

items.en: Medius plus dies produced meridies, 'midday, and by extension the south', since the sun at noon stands toward the south in the northern hemisphere.
items.cn: medius 加 dies 构成 meridies，意为「正午」，并引申为「南方」，因为北半球正午太阳位于南方。

items.en: Meridianus meant 'of midday or of the south'; this adjective passed through French and became the English noun meridian.
items.cn: meridianus 意为「正午的、南方的」；这个形容词经法语演变为英语名词 meridian。

items.en: English meridian appears in the fourteenth century for noon and for the north-south line; the geographical reference sense developed in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语 meridian 在 14 世纪出现，指正午与南北方向的线；作为经度参考的用法在 16 至 17 世纪发展起来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the acupuncture sense is a modern translation choice, and its exact first English use is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：经络义属现代翻译选择，其在英语中的确切首见年代未见记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like meridian; group two holds the lines, times and peaks it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近 meridian 的词；第二组是容易与它混淆的线、时刻与顶点概念。

entries.definition: From medius 'middle': the middle value in a set or a line through a midpoint, with no noon meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 medius「中间」：一组数的中间值或过中点的线，不含正午义。

entries.definition: The middle size or a means of communication; it shares medius but not the day.
entries.definitionCN: 指中等尺寸或媒介；同出 medius，但与「日」无关。

entries.definition: The adjective from meridian in its 'south' sense: southern, or running north-south.
entries.definitionCN: 由 meridian 的「南方」义变来的形容词：南方的，或南北走向的。

entries.definition: An uncommon variant spelling of meridional; standard usage prefers meridional.
entries.definitionCN: meridional 的罕见异体拼写；标准用法多用 meridional。

entries.definition: The east-west angle measured from a meridian; a meridian is the line, longitude is the number.
entries.definitionCN: 相对某子午线量出的东西角度；meridian 是线，longitude 是数值。

entries.definition: A latitude circle running east-west; it crosses meridians at right angles.
entries.definitionCN: 东西走向的纬线圈，与子午线正交。

entries.definition: The middle of the day, when the sun is highest; meridian can name the same moment formally.
entries.definitionCN: 一天的正中、太阳最高之时；meridian 可正式地指同一时刻。

entries.definition: The point directly overhead, or figuratively the peak; the meridian passes through it.
entries.definitionCN: 头顶正上方的点，或比喻的顶点；子午圈经过它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin 'middle day', real navigation and real astronomy, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「一日之中」、真实的航海与真实的天文学，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Medius 'middle' + dies 'day': midday, then the north-south line the noon sun crosses.
normal.cn: medius「中间」+ dies「日」：正午，再指正午太阳经过的南北向线。

normal.en: A meridian runs north-south; longitude is counted east and west from one chosen meridian.
normal.cn: 子午线南北走向；经度从选定的那条本初子午线向东西计数。

normal.en: Ante meridiem and post meridiem are the Latin phrases behind a.m. and p.m.
normal.cn: ante meridiem 与 post meridiem 就是 a.m. 与 p.m. 背后的拉丁短语。

normal.en: The sun culminates, or crosses the meridian, at local noon.
normal.cn: 太阳在当地正午达到中天，也就是经过子午圈。

normal.en: Acupuncture meridians are channels, a metaphorical line running through the body.
normal.cn: 针灸经络是通道，像一条穿过身体的比喻之线。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow shrinking to nothing as the sun stands overhead.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳当顶时影子缩到几乎没有。

abstract.en: Picture a career that has reached its noon and can only move sideways.
abstract.cn: 想象一项事业已到正午，此后只能横向移动。

abstract.en: Picture a seam down the middle of a sphere, joining both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从球体正中穿过、连接两端的接缝。

examples.en: The prime meridian passes through Greenwich.
examples.cn: 本初子午线穿过格林尼治。

examples.en: The ship's chronometer was set to the meridian of Greenwich.
examples.cn: 船上的航海钟按格林尼治子午线设定。

examples.en: His career reached its meridian in the 1990s.
examples.cn: 他的事业在二十世纪九十年代达到顶点。

dict_mnemonic.text: meri（中间，如 medium）+ dian（日，如 diary 每日）→ 一日之中 → 正午、子午线

root: 拉丁 meridies「正午、南方」= medius「中间」+ dies「日」；meridianus「正午的、南方的」经法语进入英语，兼指正午与南北向大圆。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from 'middle of the day': the north-south line the noon sun crosses, the zero line chosen for longitude, the hour of noon, the sun's culmination, the peak of a career, the body's channels, the sky's north-south circle, and the transit across it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「一日之中」出发：正午太阳经过的南北线、被选作经度零点的线、正午时刻、太阳中天、事业顶点、身体通道、天球南北圈，以及越过它的事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the noon sun standing on an invisible north-south circle that runs through both poles and the observer's zenith.
core.cn: 核心意象：正午的太阳立在一条看不见的南北大圆上，这条圆穿过两极与观测者天顶。

branches.en: THE LINE: the earth and the sky each draw the same north-south great circle.
branches.cn: 线：地球与天空各自画出同一条南北大圆。

branches.en: ZERO BY AGREEMENT: one meridian is chosen as the zero for all the others.
branches.cn: 约定的零度：选一条子午线作为其余各线的零点。

branches.en: THE MOMENT: noon, the sun's culmination and the star's transit are the same crossing seen as time.
branches.cn: 时刻：正午、太阳中天与恒星中天，是同一次穿越在时间上的呈现。

branches.en: THE PEAK: a career at its height is the noon sun applied to a life.
branches.cn: 顶点：事业的高处，就是正午太阳用于人生。

branches.en: THE BODY: a channel running through the body borrows the line's shape.
branches.cn: 身体：贯穿身体的通道借用了线的形态。

intro.en: Meridian is built from Latin words for 'middle' and 'day'; the same parts survive in midday, medius and the a.m./p.m. phrases.
intro.cn: meridian 由拉丁的「中间」与「日」两个词构成；同样的成分保存在 midday、medius 与 a.m./p.m. 短语中。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius 'middle' and dies 'day' combine in meridies 'midday'; meridies yields meridianus and the English meridian, while medius also gives median and medium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 medius「中间」与 dies「日」组合成 meridies「正午」；meridies 衍生 meridianus 与英语 meridian，而 medius 还衍生 median 与 medium。

items.example: The root marks the centre of the day.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根标出一日之中。

items.example: The second element names the day itself.
At noon the sun stands toward the south.
The adjective became the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词变成了英语名词。

items.example: The map marks every tenth meridian.
items.exampleCN: 地图每隔十条经线标一条。

definition_zh: 优点；长处；价值；功绩；值得
definition_en: a good quality that deserves praise; the real worth of something; a record of service that earns reward; and as a verb, to deserve something
core_image: 桌上摊着一份朴素的工作记录，密密麻麻的小字压过了封面上那个显赫的姓氏
scene: 评审室里只摆着几份匿名材料，桌上没有名片，也没有介绍人，评委们一页页翻过去，在纸边写下批注。The panel chose the plainest proposal on merit alone.
sceneCN: 这里是「优点、真才实学」（第 1 个义项：值得称赞的长处）；句意为评审只凭方案自身的优点，选中了最朴素的那一份。图中可辨识物件：匿名材料、批注笔迹、空着的名片位。

pos.zh: 优点；长处；价值；功绩
值得；应得

derivatives.zh: 由 merit 加 -orious 构成，义为「值得称赞的；有功绩的」
由 merit 与 -cracy（统治）复合而成，义为「精英治理；唯才是举的制度」
由 de-（减损）加 merit 构成，义为「缺点；过失」
由 merit 加 -ed 构成，义为「应得的；理所应当的」

senses.title: A good quality that deserves praise
senses.definition: a quality or feature of a person or thing that is good and deserves to be praised
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物身上值得称赞的好品质、好特点
senses.example: The plan's main merit is that it costs almost nothing to run.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案最大的优点几乎不花钱就能运转。
senses.why: Latin meritum named what a person had earned, so the first sense of the word is the good thing in someone that makes praise seem earned rather than given.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 meritum 指一个人挣得、应得的东西，所以这个词的第一层含义就是人身上那处让人不得不称赞的好处——称赞像是被挣来的，而不是白送的。

senses.title: The real worth of something
senses.definition: the actual worth or value of something, weighed when people judge whether it is any good
senses.definitionCN: 事物本身的实际价值，是人们在判断好坏时所称量的东西
senses.example: The judges compared the merits of the two designs before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 评委在投票前比较了两个设计各自的价值。
senses.why: Once merit means what is deserved, judging a thing on merit means setting aside the label and weighing what it can really do.
senses.whyCN: 既然 merit 指「应得之物」，那么按 merit 评判一事物，就是把招牌放到一边，只称量它真正能做到什么。

senses.title: A record that earns reward or honour
senses.definition: the accumulated record of good service or achievement that makes a person deserve reward, promotion or public honour
senses.definitionCN: 长期积累的良好服务或成绩，使人有资格获得奖赏、晋升或公开表彰
senses.example: Years of quiet merit finally brought her the senior post.
senses.exampleCN: 多年默默积累的功绩终于让她得到了那个高级职位。
senses.why: Because merit is something earned, it can be counted over time, and a long count of good work turns into the sense of service that a medal or a promotion answers.
senses.whyCN: 因为 merit 是挣来的东西，它可以随时间累积；长期积累的好工作就变成「功劳」这一层含义，奖章或晋升正是对它的回应。

senses.title: To deserve something
senses.definition: to be worth something, or to have earned attention, praise, punishment or serious consideration
senses.definitionCN: 够得上某物，或已经挣得注意、称赞、惩罚或认真对待的资格
senses.example: The question merits a careful answer rather than a quick guess.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题值得认真作答，而不该随手猜一句。
senses.why: The verb keeps the oldest Latin meaning almost untouched: merere was to earn, so to merit something is to have already earned it and therefore to deserve it.
senses.whyCN: 动词义几乎原样保留了拉丁语 merere 最古老的意思「挣得」：to merit 某物，就是已经把它挣到手，因此「值得」。

intro.en: Merit goes back to a Latin verb for earning, and the noun for the thing earned passed through French into English, where it became both a quality and a verb of deserving.
intro.cn: merit 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「挣得」的动词，指「挣得之物」的名词经法语进入英语，后来既是优点，也作「值得」的动词。

items.en: Merere meant to earn, to gain by service, and it already carried the idea that pay follows work.
items.cn: merere 意为挣得、靠出力获得，本身已带着「先有付出、后有回报」的意思。

items.en: Meritum was the noun for what had been earned or deserved, whether a wage, a reward or a good name.
items.cn: meritum 是名词，指挣得或应得的东西，可以是工钱、奖赏，也可以是好名声。

items.en: Old French took the Latin noun as merite, meaning worth, value or a deserving act, and used it in both praise and blame.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁名词写作 merite，意为价值、长处或值得称道的行为，褒贬两边都用。

items.en: Middle English merit named a quality worth praising and also the state of being entitled to a reward.
items.cn: 中古英语的 merit 既指值得称赞的品质，也指有资格获得奖赏的状态。

items.en: Modern English added the verb sense of deserving and kept the phrase on merit for judging without favour.
items.cn: 现代英语补上动词「值得」的用法，并保留 on merit 这一说法，指不带偏私地评判。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Latin earning family, including a prefixed word that reverses the value; the near-meaning group collects words for goodness and worth.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「挣得」词族，其中包括一个把价值反过来、加了前缀的词；近义组收表示良善与价值的词。

entries.definition: Deserving praise because of good work or service.
entries.definitionCN: 因出色的工作或贡献而值得称赞的。

entries.definition: A system in which power belongs to those who have earned it by ability.
entries.definitionCN: 权力归于凭才能挣得位置者的制度。

entries.definition: A fault or failing that counts against a person, the opposite of a merit.
entries.definitionCN: 记在人账上的缺点或过失，与优点相对。

entries.definition: Earned and therefore justly given, as of praise or punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 因挣得而应当给予的，用于称赞或惩罚。

entries.definition: A morally good quality in a person, especially one long practised.
entries.definitionCN: 人身上道德上的好品质，尤指长期养成的。

entries.definition: The true value of a thing, measured apart from its price or label.
entries.definitionCN: 事物真正的价值，不以价钱或标签衡量。

entries.definition: The importance or usefulness that something has for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 某物对某个用途的重要性或用处。

entries.definition: A quality a person or thing is good at, seen as a resource.
entries.definitionCN: 人或事物擅长的那一处品质，被看作可用的资源。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for earning; the family keeps returning to what is earned, what deserves praise and what can therefore be taken away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「挣得」的动词上，同族词反复回到挣得之物、值得称赞之处，以及因而已可被拿走的东西。

normal.en: Merere in Latin means to earn, so merit is not a gift but a balance built up by work.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merere 意为挣得，所以 merit 不是白送的礼，而是靠工作一点点攒出来的余额。

normal.en: Meritum is the thing earned, which is why the English noun can mean both a good quality and a record of service.
normal.cn: meritum 指挣得之物，所以英语名词既能指好品质，也能指功劳记录。

normal.en: Meritorious adds -orious and says a person or an act is full of merit.
normal.cn: meritorious 加 -orious，表示某人或某事充满 merit。

normal.en: Demerit adds de-, which takes value away, so the word names a fault instead of a virtue.
normal.cn: demerit 加 de-，把价值减掉，于是这个词指过失而不是美德。

normal.en: Meritocracy joins merit to -cracy, rule by those who have earned the right to rule.
normal.cn: meritocracy 把 merit 与 -cracy 组合，指由挣得统治资格者来统治。

abstract.en: A word for earned value suggests that praise is not something handed out but something a person has already paid for in effort.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「挣得价值」的词说明：称赞不是随手发的，而是人已经用力气付过账的。

abstract.en: Judging on merit asks a hard question, what would remain of this person if the name and the uniform were removed.
abstract.cn: 按 merit 评判要回答一个难题：若去掉姓名与制服，这个人还剩下什么。

abstract.en: Because merit can be counted and also taken away, the word quietly holds both fairness and the fear of losing it.
abstract.cn: 因为 merit 既能累积也能被扣掉，这个词同时装着公平，以及失去公平的忧虑。

examples.en: The panel judged the entries on merit alone.
examples.cn: 评审只看作品本身的长处。

examples.en: The proposal merits a second reading.
examples.cn: 这项提议值得再读一遍。

examples.en: Her merit was recognized long before the title arrived.
examples.cn: 早在头衔到来之前，她的功劳就已被看见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖力特」——肯卖力气的人特别值得称赞；记住 merit 是优点、值得。

root: 拉丁语 merere（挣得、应得）派生出 meritum（应得之物），经古法语 merite 进入英语；同族词多与功绩、应得、褒贬有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what has been earned and therefore deserves praise; the senses divide into a good quality, a thing's real worth, a record of service and the verb of deserving.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「挣得因而应得」；义项由此分出值得称赞的长处、事物本身的价值、功劳记录，以及动词「值得」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain work record lying open on a table, its long column of small entries outweighing the famous name on the cover.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊着一份朴素的工作记录，密密麻麻的小字压过了封面上那个显赫的姓氏。

branches.en: a quiet colleague whose steady work everyone trusts
branches.cn: 一位沉默的同事，靠稳定的工作赢得所有人的信任

branches.en: a plain design chosen over a glossy one
branches.cn: 朴素的设计胜过花哨的设计

branches.en: a judge weighing a plan with the price tag turned face down
branches.cn: 评审把价签翻过去，只称量方案本身

branches.en: a long service record read aloud at a ceremony
branches.cn: 典礼上被高声念出的一长串功绩记录

branches.en: a question that makes the whole room go quiet
branches.cn: 一个让全场安静下来的问题

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of earning, its noun for the thing earned, the French form, and English endings that build an adjective, a fault and a system.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示挣得的拉丁动词、指挣得之物的名词、法语形式，以及构成形容词、过失词与制度词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 欢乐的；愉快的；喜庆的；微醺的
definition_en: cheerful and full of lively fun; also used of holidays and celebrations to wish joy, and in informal British use, pleasantly drunk
core_image: 壁炉火旺的冬夜，一家人围着桌子唱歌，窗上贴满手剪的雪花
scene: 壁炉里的柴火烧得正旺，窗上贴着手剪的雪花，孩子们正把彩纸环挂上门框。The whole room felt merry as the family sang together.
sceneCN: 这里是「欢乐的、愉快的」（第 1 个义项：心情欢快）；句意为全家人一起唱歌时，整个屋子都显得喜气洋洋。图中可辨识物件：壁炉、纸雪花、彩纸环。

pos.zh: 欢乐的；愉快的；喜庆的；微醺的

derivatives.zh: 由 merry 去 y 加 -ment 构成，义为「欢乐；欢闹」
由 merry 去 y 加 -ly 构成，义为「欢快地；愉快地」
由 merry 与 making 复合而成，义为「欢庆；作乐」

senses.title: Cheerful and full of lively fun
senses.definition: cheerful, happy and full of lively fun, especially when people are together
senses.definitionCN: 高兴、快活、充满热闹的乐趣，尤指与人相处时
senses.example: The children grew merry as the music started.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐一响，孩子们就快活起来。
senses.why: Old English myrige meant pleasing and agreeable, so the earliest sense is not loud laughter but a mood that feels good to be inside.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 myrige 意为「令人愉快的、合意的」，所以最早的意思不是放声大笑，而是一种让人觉得舒服、愿意待在其中的心境。

senses.title: Lively and festive, as of a holiday
senses.definition: used of holidays and celebrations to wish someone joy, as in the fixed greeting for Christmas
senses.definitionCN: 用于节日与庆祝场合，向人道贺，如圣诞节的固定祝语
senses.example: They hung coloured lights and wished every neighbour a merry Christmas.
senses.exampleCN: 他们挂起彩灯，向每位邻居道一声圣诞快乐。
senses.why: Once a feast is a shared good time, the word attaches itself to the day rather than to the feeling, and ends up fixed inside holiday greetings.
senses.whyCN: 当宴饮成了众人共享的好时光，这个词就黏到日子本身上，而不只是心情，最后被固定进节日祝语里。

senses.title: Slightly drunk and cheerful
senses.definition: in informal British use, pleasantly drunk and therefore more talkative and cheerful than usual
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中指喝得恰到好处、因而比平时更爱说笑的状态
senses.example: After two glasses of wine he was merry but still polite.
senses.exampleCN: 两杯酒下肚，他有了些酒意，却仍旧有礼。
senses.why: Drink lowers the guard, so the cheerfulness the word already names turns into the visible, glass-in-hand kind that loosens the tongue.
senses.whyCN: 酒放松了戒备，于是这个词本来就指的欢快，变成一种看得见、手上有杯子、会松开舌头的热闹。

intro.en: Merry belongs to the Germanic side of English and goes back to an Old English adjective meaning pleasing; no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
intro.cn: merry 属于英语中的日耳曼语这一支，可追溯到意为「令人愉快的」的古英语形容词；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed adjective meaning agreeable or pleasant lay behind the word; scholars generally link it to a root for short, with the idea of time passing pleasantly.
items.cn: 这个词背后是一个重构的形容词，意为「合意的、令人愉快的」；一般认为它与表示「短」的词根有关，即时光短而愉快。

items.en: Myrige meant pleasing, delightful and agreeable, and it described places, sounds and company as much as people.
items.cn: myrige 意为令人愉快的、可爱的、合意的，既能形容人，也能形容地方、声音与同伴。

items.en: Middle English mery narrowed toward cheerful and lively, and the spelling settled on merry in the north.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mery 收窄为「快活、有生气」，拼写最终在北方定为 merry。

items.en: From the idea of a loosened, cheerful mood came the informal sense of pleasantly drunk, which stayed common in British speech.
items.cn: 从「心情松弛、快活」这一想法，引申出「微醺」的口语义，这个用法在英式英语中一直常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps merry mostly in fixed greetings and set phrases, while everyday cheerfulness is usually carried by other words.
items.cn: 现代英语里 merry 多保留在固定祝语与成语中，日常的「快活」通常由别的词来承担。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the merry family plus one word that only shares the sound; the near-meaning group collects words for cheer, jollity and celebration.
note.cn: 形近组收 merry 的词族，另加一个只是读音相近的词；近义组收表示快活、热闹与喜庆的词。

entries.definition: Lively fun and laughter shared by a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一群人共享的热闹与笑声。

entries.definition: In a cheerful, lively way.
entries.definitionCN: 以欢快、有生气的方式。

entries.definition: The act of celebrating noisily and happily.
entries.definitionCN: 热热闹闹地庆祝的行为。

entries.definition: Only the sound is close; this verb means to become husband and wife, with no shared origin.
entries.definitionCN: 只是读音相近，这个词意为结婚，词源并不相同。

entries.definition: Showing good spirits, often as a steady habit rather than a burst of fun.
entries.definitionCN: 显得心情好，常是稳定的性情，而非一阵热闹。

entries.definition: Full of deep gladness, stronger and more inward than mere high spirits.
entries.definitionCN: 充满深切喜悦，比单纯兴致高更强烈、更内在。

entries.definition: Good-humoured and sociable, often with a hearty, slightly loud manner.
entries.definitionCN: 脾气温和、爱交际，常带爽朗而略响亮的派头。

entries.definition: Belonging to a feast or holiday, marked by decoration and celebration.
entries.definitionCN: 属于节庆的，以装点与庆祝为特征。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from an Old English adjective for what feels agreeable; its family keeps the shared good time, the laughter around it and the greetings it ended up inside.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自一个意为「令人觉得合意」的古英语形容词，同族词保留着共享的好时光、身旁的笑声，以及它最后被装进去的祝语。

normal.en: Myrige in Old English meant pleasing, so merry began as a good feeling rather than as noise.
normal.cn: 古英语 myrige 意为令人愉快，所以 merry 起初是一种好心情，而不是吵闹。

normal.en: The comparative is merrier, not more merry, because the word is short and old enough for the -er ending.
normal.cn: 比较级是 merrier 而不是 more merry，因为这个词又短又古老，够得上用 -er 词尾。

normal.en: Merriment adds -ment and turns the adjective into the shared state of being merry.
normal.cn: merriment 加 -ment，把形容词变成一种共享的「欢闹状态」。

normal.en: Merrily adds -ly, and the doubled r keeps the short e sound of merry.
normal.cn: merrily 加 -ly，双写的 r 保住了 merry 里短促的 e 音。

normal.en: Merry is now locked inside greetings such as Merry Christmas, which outlived most of its free uses.
normal.cn: merry 如今被锁在 Merry Christmas 这类祝语里，而这些祝语比它大多数自由用法活得更久。

abstract.en: A word for a pleasant mood ended up naming a whole season, which shows how a feeling can attach itself to a date on the calendar.
abstract.cn: 一个表示愉快心情的词最后指整个节季，这说明一种感受可以黏到日历上的某个日子上。

abstract.en: Merry lives mostly in greetings now, a reminder that some words survive by being said at the right moment.
abstract.cn: merry 如今多活在祝语里，提醒人有些词是靠「在对的时刻说出来」而存活的。

abstract.en: The same word can mean happy and slightly drunk, because both describe a guard that has been let down.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指快活又能指微醺，因为两者都描述一道被放下的戒备。

examples.en: The room grew merry as the fire caught and the singing began.
examples.cn: 火苗窜起、歌声响起时，屋子里渐渐欢腾起来。

examples.en: They wished the old man a merry Christmas and left a small parcel.
examples.cn: 他们祝老人圣诞快乐，留下一个小包裹。

examples.en: Two cups of hot wine made him merry enough to tell stories.
examples.cn: 两杯热酒下肚，他高兴得讲起了故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「玛丽」——节日里人人喊着玛丽，满街欢腾；记住 merry 是欢乐的。

root: 古英语 myrige（令人愉快的）来自原始日耳曼语重构形式 *murgijaz，一般认为与表示「短」的词根有关，即时光短而愉快；细节仍有不同说法，无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mood that feels good to be in; the senses spread to the festive day, the holiday greeting and the loosened cheer that comes with drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种待着舒服的好心情；义项扩到喜庆的日子、节日祝语，以及酒意带来的松弛欢快。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire burning high on a winter night, a family singing round the table, hand-cut snowflakes stuck to the window.
core.cn: 核心意象：冬夜壁炉火旺，一家人围着桌子唱歌，窗上贴满手剪的雪花。

branches.en: children laughing as the music starts
branches.cn: 音乐响起时笑成一团的孩子

branches.en: a table crowded with relatives and warm plates
branches.cn: 围满亲人、摆着热菜的桌子

branches.en: a paper greeting pinned above a door
branches.cn: 门楣上贴着的节日祝语

branches.en: two glasses on a table and a loosened tie
branches.cn: 桌上两只杯子与松开的领带

branches.en: a party where greetings and wine run together
branches.cn: 祝语与酒意混在一起的聚会

intro.en: The word is carried by an Old English adjective, its Middle English respelling, two English endings and a noun suffix; it has no reliable Latin cognate.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语形容词、中古英语拼写、两个英语词尾与一个名词后缀共同支撑；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for merry: the word belongs to the Germanic branch, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: merry 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它属于日耳曼语这一支，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

definition_zh: 混乱；脏乱；污物；困境；弄乱；食堂
definition_en: an untidy or dirty state; the waste left behind; a difficult situation; a group of people who eat together or the room where they eat; and as a verb, to make untidy or to spoil
core_image: 聚餐散场后，桌上盘盏堆叠，汤汁洒在桌布上，地上散落着碎屑
scene: 聚餐散场后，桌上的盘子还堆着，地毯上撒了饼干屑，厨房的门半开着。After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
sceneCN: 这里是「凌乱、脏乱」（第 1 个义项：东西没归位）；句意为聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。图中可辨识物件：堆着的盘子、地毯上的碎屑、半开的门。

pos.zh: 混乱；脏乱；污物；困境；食堂
弄乱；搞砸

derivatives.zh: 由 mess 加 -y 构成，义为「凌乱的；脏乱的」
由 messy 去 y 加 -ly 构成，义为「凌乱地」
由 messy 去 y 加 -ness 构成，义为「凌乱；杂乱」

senses.title: An untidy, dirty state
senses.definition: a state in which things are not in order and look dirty or untidy
senses.definitionCN: 东西没有归位、看上去又脏又乱的状态
senses.example: After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
senses.exampleCN: 聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。
senses.why: The earliest mess was a portion of food served at table, so the modern sense of disorder still smells of the kitchen: plates, scraps and things left where they fell.
senses.whyCN: 最早的 mess 是端上桌的一份食物，所以今天「凌乱」这一义仍带着厨房气味：盘子、残渣，以及掉在哪里就留在哪里的东西。

senses.title: Dirt or waste left behind
senses.definition: dirty waste matter, especially the droppings of an animal, that somebody has to clean away
senses.definitionCN: 脏的废弃物，尤指动物的粪便，需要有人清理掉
senses.example: Watch the path, the dog leaves a mess on the grass every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 走路当心，那条狗每天早上都在草地上留下一摊脏东西。
senses.why: Once a mess is food that has been served and eaten, what remains on the ground is also a mess, so the word slides from the meal to its leftovers and then to any filth.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mess 是端上桌又被吃掉的食物，留在地上的残渣自然也是 mess，于是词义从饭菜滑向剩渣，再滑向一切脏东西。

senses.title: A difficult or confused situation
senses.definition: a situation full of trouble and confusion, especially one that someone has caused and must get out of
senses.definitionCN: 充满麻烦与混乱的局面，尤指自己造成、又必须脱身的局面
senses.example: He admitted his finances were in a mess after the failed deal.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认那笔交易失败后，自己的财务状况一团糟。
senses.why: When things are physically out of order, affairs can be out of order too, so the untidy room grows into a tangled situation with no easy way out.
senses.whyCN: 当东西在实处乱了套，事情也能乱套，于是凌乱的房间长成一团找不到出口的局面。

senses.title: To make untidy or to spoil
senses.definition: to make something dirty or untidy, or to spoil a plan or arrangement badly
senses.definitionCN: 把东西弄脏弄乱，或把计划、安排彻底毁掉
senses.example: He messed up the schedule by moving two meetings without telling anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他没打招呼就挪动了两个会议，把日程搞乱了。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act: to put something into a mess, or to ruin it the way a spilled plate ruins a laid table.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：把东西弄成一团乱，或者像打翻一盘菜弄污摆好的桌面那样，把事情毁掉。

senses.title: A group that eats together, or its dining room
senses.definition: a group of people, especially soldiers, who eat together, or the room in which they eat
senses.definitionCN: 一起吃饭的一群人，尤指军人，或他们就餐的房间
senses.example: The officers gathered in the mess before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军官们在黎明前聚到食堂。
senses.why: The first sense was a portion of food shared at one table; the people who shared it and the room where they shared it then took over the same name.
senses.whyCN: 最初的意思是同桌分享的一份食物；一起分享的人，以及他们分享所在的房间，后来都沿用了这个名字。

intro.en: Mess began as a word for a portion of food sent to table, and it reached English through French from a Latin verb meaning to send.
intro.cn: mess 起初指端上桌的一份食物，经法语进入英语，其源头是拉丁语中表示「送」的动词。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it supplied the verb behind a large family of sending words.
items.cn: mittere 意为送、放出，是这一大批与「送」有关的词共同的动词来源。

items.en: The noun missus named a course of food served at a meal, literally something sent to the table.
items.cn: 名词 missus 指用餐时端上的一道菜，字面意思是「被送到桌上的东西」。

items.en: Old French mes kept the food sense, meaning a portion or a dish, and also a group eating together.
items.cn: 古法语 mes 保留了食物义，指一份或一道菜，也可指一起进餐的一群人。

items.en: Middle English mess first meant a dish of food and a company of diners, especially in a household or an army.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mess 先指一盘食物和一群共餐者，尤用于家庭或军队。

items.en: Modern English pushed the word toward disorder in the eighteenth century, while the dining sense survived in military usage.
items.cn: 现代英语在十八世纪把词义推向「混乱」，而就餐义则在军队用语中保存下来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same Latin sending root; the near-meaning group collects words for disorder and jumble.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「送」词根上的词；近义组收表示混乱与杂乱的名词。

entries.definition: Untidy, dirty or complicated, said of rooms, hair or situations.
entries.definitionCN: 凌乱的、脏的或复杂的，可用于房间、头发或局面。

entries.definition: A piece of information sent to someone, from the same verb of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 送给某人的一条信息，同出「送」这一动词。

entries.definition: A person who carries a message from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 把消息从一处送到另一处的人。

entries.definition: An object thrown or fired, literally something sent.
entries.definitionCN: 被投出或射出的物体，字面即「被送出的东西」。

entries.definition: A lack of order, often on a larger scale than a messy room.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏秩序，范围常比凌乱的房间更大。

entries.definition: A mass of small things lying about and taking up space.
entries.definitionCN: 散乱堆放着、占地方的一堆小东西。

entries.definition: Complete confusion in which nothing can be controlled.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底失控的混乱。

entries.definition: A confused mixture or a state of muddled thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 混杂的一团，或思路不清的状态。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of sending; its family keeps returning to food sent to a table, the people around it, and the disorder left when the meal ends.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「送」的动词上，同族词反复回到端上桌的食物、围桌的人，以及餐后留下的凌乱。

normal.en: Mittere in Latin means to send, and missus was a dish sent to the table.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为送，missus 就是被送到桌上的一道菜。

normal.en: Old French mes kept the food sense, so English mess first meant a portion or a dish, not a dirty room.
normal.cn: 古法语 mes 保留食物义，所以英语 mess 起初指一份或一道菜，而不是脏屋子。

normal.en: Because diners shared one dish, mess also named the group and the room where they ate, a sense still used in the army.
normal.cn: 因为同桌分食，mess 也指共餐的一群人与他们就餐的房间，这一义在军队中仍在用。

normal.en: Messy adds -y, meaning full of mess, and therefore untidy.
normal.cn: messy 加 -y，意为「充满 mess」，因此是凌乱的。

normal.en: Mess up is the verb phrase that turns the noun into the act of spoiling something.
normal.cn: mess up 这一动词短语把名词变成「把事情毁掉」的动作。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a shared dish now means disorder, which suggests mess is always what a good meal leaves behind.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经指共享菜食的词如今指混乱，这说明混乱往往是一顿好饭留下的残局。

abstract.en: The same word covers the food, the people eating it and the room they sit in, three parts of one ordinary evening.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖了食物、吃饭的人与他们坐的房间，这是一个寻常夜晚的三个部分。

abstract.en: Calling a situation a mess borrows the picture of a table after dinner, because trouble is easier to bear when it looks like crumbs.
abstract.cn: 把局面称作 mess，是借用了餐后桌面的画面，因为麻烦一旦看起来像碎屑，就比较好承受。

examples.en: After the dinner party, the kitchen was a complete mess.
examples.cn: 聚餐结束后，厨房一片狼藉。

examples.en: He messed up the schedule by moving two meetings without telling anyone.
examples.cn: 他没打招呼就挪动了两个会议，把日程搞乱了。

examples.en: The officers gathered in the mess before dawn.
examples.cn: 军官们在黎明前聚到食堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没洗」——碗没洗，厨房就乱成一团；记住 mess 是混乱。

root: 拉丁语 mittere（送）的分词名词 missus 指「端上桌的一道菜」，经古法语 mes（一份食物）进入英语；先指食物与共餐，后引申为凌乱与困境。

sensesIntro.en: The core is food sent to a shared table; the senses spread from the meal to its leftovers, then to disorder, to a troubled situation and to the room where a group eats.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是送到共享桌上的一份食物；义项从饭菜扩到残渣，再到凌乱、困境，以及一群人吃饭的房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table after a party, plates stacked high, gravy spilt on the cloth and crumbs scattered across the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚餐散场后的桌面，盘盏高高堆起，汤汁洒在桌布上，碎屑散落一地。

branches.en: a sink piled with plates after a party
branches.cn: 聚餐后堆满盘子的水池

branches.en: crumbs and greasy marks across a table
branches.cn: 满桌碎屑与油痕

branches.en: a shoe scraping something off the grass
branches.cn: 鞋底在草地上蹭掉脏东西

branches.en: a desk buried under unsigned papers
branches.cn: 被未签文件埋住的办公桌

branches.en: a tray dropped at the door of a dining room
branches.cn: 食堂门口打翻的托盘

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of sending, its noun for a dish served, the French form, and English endings that build an adjective and a noun of state.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「送」的拉丁动词、指上桌菜食的名词、法语形式，以及构成形容词与状态名词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
