senses.title: A way of doing something
senses.titleCN: 方法：做某事的特定路数
senses.definition: a particular procedure for doing something, especially a planned and systematic one
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的特定程序，尤指有计划、有系统的程序
senses.example: The lab still uses a method that has not changed in forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验室仍在使用一套四十年没变过的方法。
senses.why: Method reached English in the early 15th century from Greek methodos, originally 'pursuit, a following after'. A method is a path that has already been walked and can be walked again.
senses.whyCN: method 于 15 世纪初从希腊语 methodos 进入英语，原义为“追寻、跟随其后”。方法就是一条已经被人走过、还可以再走一遍的路。

senses.title: Orderliness
senses.definition: the quality of acting in an orderly, systematic way rather than at random
senses.definitionCN: 做事有条理、有系统，而非随意的品质
senses.example: There was method in the way she sorted the files, though no one else could see it.
senses.exampleCN: 她整理文件的方式自有章法，只是别人看不出来。
senses.why: From the 1610s the word also named 'orderliness, regularity'. The path is no longer a particular route but the habit of always walking on one.
senses.whyCN: 自 17 世纪 10 年代起，这个词也指“有条理、有规律”。此时路不再是一条具体路线，而是“总要沿着某条路走”的习惯。

senses.title: A complete system
senses.definition: a complete set of rules or procedures for attaining an end
senses.definitionCN: 为达到某一目的而设的一整套规则或程序
senses.example: The school adopted a new method for teaching reading.
senses.exampleCN: 学校采用了一套新的阅读教学体系。
senses.why: The sense 'a system or complete set of rules' is recorded from the 1680s. Once a path is written down as rules, it can be taught to strangers.
senses.whyCN: “体系或完整规则集”这一义项自 17 世纪 80 年代有记录。一旦一条路被写成规则，它就能教给陌生人。

senses.title: Scientific method
senses.titleCN: 科学方法：学科自己的路
senses.definition: the established procedure of a discipline for testing claims and producing knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科为检验主张、生产知识而确立的程序
senses.example: The scientific method is less a single recipe than a set of habits of doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 科学方法与其说是一份单一配方，不如说是一组怀疑的习惯。
senses.why: Greek methodos already meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry'. Science did not invent the word; it inherited the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 methodos 本就意为“科学探究、探究的方法”。科学没有发明这个词，它继承的是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Teaching and acting methods
senses.titleCN: 教学法与表演体系：一门手艺的路
senses.definition: a named system of practice in teaching or in the arts, such as the direct method or method acting
senses.definitionCN: 教学或艺术中以人名或特征命名的实践体系，如直接教学法、方法派表演
senses.example: Method acting asks the performer to draw on real memories.
senses.exampleCN: 方法派表演要求演员调动真实的记忆。
senses.why: A system with a name becomes a school. Method here is a path that a whole profession agrees to walk together.
senses.whyCN: 一套有名字的体系会变成一派。这里的 method 是一整门行业同意一起走的那条路。

senses.title: Old medical sense
senses.titleCN: 医学旧义：系统化的治疗方案
senses.definition: in early use, the regular, systematic treatment of disease
senses.definitionCN: 在早期用法中，指对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗
senses.example: The medieval physician spoke of a method for fevers, not a single remedy.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的医生讲的是治疗热病的一套方法，而不是某一味药。
senses.why: The first English sense, in the early 15th century, was 'regular, systematic treatment of disease'. The word entered through medicine before it belonged to everything else.
senses.whyCN: 英语中的第一个义项是 15 世纪初的“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”。这个词先通过医学进来，然后才属于一切别的事物。

senses.title: Method in programming
senses.titleCN: 编程中的方法：对象身上的函数
senses.definition: in object-oriented programming, a function or procedure attached to an object or class
senses.definitionCN: 在面向对象编程中，附着于对象或类上的函数或过程
senses.example: The method returns a new list instead of changing the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法返回一个新列表，而不修改旧列表。
senses.why: The metaphor survives in code: a method is still a fixed route the object knows how to take when it is called.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻在代码里活了下来：方法仍是对象被调用时知道该怎么走的一条固定路线。

senses.title: A method of inquiry
senses.titleCN: 探究之路：哲学意义上的方法
senses.definition: in philosophy, the deliberate path of doubt or reasoning by which a conclusion is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中，为抵达结论而有意采取的怀疑或推理之路
senses.example: Descartes began with a method of doubt that would leave only certainty standing.
senses.exampleCN: 笛卡尔从一种怀疑的方法开始，只为留下确定的东西。
senses.why: Methodos was literally a following after something. Philosophy turns that pursuit into a rule for how to pursue anything at all.
senses.whyCN: methodos 字面上就是“跟在某物之后追”。哲学把这趟追寻变成一条规则，规定该怎样追寻任何东西。

senses.title: Method in one's madness
senses.definition: in the phrase 'there is method in one's madness', used when apparently foolish behaviour turns out to have a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 「there is method in one's madness」 中，指看似荒唐的行为其实自有目的
senses.example: He shuffles the cards for ten minutes, but there is method in his madness.
senses.exampleCN: 他把牌洗了十分钟，看似荒唐，其实自有章法。
senses.why: Shakespeare's phrase 'though this be madness, yet there is method in it' (Hamlet) gave English a fixed way to say that a path is hidden inside chaos.
senses.whyCN: 莎士比亚的句子“though this be madness, yet there is method in it”（《哈姆雷特》）给了英语一个固定说法：混乱里藏着一条路。

intro.en: Method is Greek: meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road, way'. Latin borrowed it as methodus and passed it to French and English. It has no connection with medical, despite the shared -met- shape. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: method 是希腊词：meta“追寻”加 hodos“路、道”。拉丁语把它借作 methodus，再传给法语和英语。尽管有共同的 -met- 外形，它与 medical 毫无关系。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'regular, systematic treatment of disease', through Latin methodus 'way of teaching or going' and Greek methodos.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 15 世纪初，意为“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”，经拉丁语 methodus“教学或行走之道”与希腊语 methodos 而来。

items.en: Greek methodos meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry, investigation', and originally 'pursuit, a following after'.
items.cn: 希腊语 methodos 意为“科学探究、探究的方法、调查”，原义为“追寻、跟随其后”。

items.en: The word joins meta 'in pursuit or quest of' and hodos 'a way, path, track, road', also 'a journey'. Hodos is of uncertain origin; Beekes suggests PIE *sod- 'course', and it is traditionally linked to Slavic words for 'course'.
items.cn: 这个词由 meta“追寻、求索”与 hodos“路、路径、轨道、道路”（也指“旅程”）组合而成。hodos 的来源不确定；Beekes 提出原始印欧语 *sod-“行程”，传统上也把它与斯拉夫语表示“行程”的词联系起来。

items.en: The sense widened to 'any way of doing anything' in the 1580s, to 'orderliness, regularity' in the 1610s, and to 'a system or complete set of rules' in the 1680s.
items.cn: 词义在 16 世纪 80 年代扩展到“做任何事的方式”，17 世纪 10 年代扩展到“有条理、有规律”，17 世纪 80 年代扩展到“体系或完整的一套规则”。

items.en: The phrase method acting is recorded in reference to the theory associated with the Russian director Konstantin Stanislavski.
items.cn: method acting 这一说法有记录，指与俄国导演康斯坦丁·斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基相关的理论。

items.en: Medical goes back to Latin medicus 'physician', with no Greek element. Meta- in method is the Greek preposition 'in pursuit of', not the modern prefix meaning 'beyond' or 'after'; the two words only share letters.
items.cn: medical 追溯到拉丁语 medicus“医生”，不含希腊语成分。method 里的 meta- 是希腊语介词“追寻”，不是现代表示“超越、之后”的前缀；两个词只共享字母。

note.en: The first group is the word family built on method: the adjective, the adverb and the study of method. The second group compares the nouns English uses for 'a way of doing something', which differ in scale and in who owns the way.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 method 上的词族：形容词、副词与研究方法的学问。第二组比较英语里表示“做某事的方式”的几个名词，区别在于尺度大小与“这条路归谁”。

entries.definition: the branch of knowledge that studies methods, or the set of methods used in a field. It is not a longer synonym of method: a methodology can contain several methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究方法的学问分支，或某一领域所使用的一套方法。它不是 method 的加长同义词：一套方法论里可以包含好几种方法。

entries.definition: done according to a method; orderly and systematic. It describes a person or a procedure, not a route.
entries.definitionCN: 按方法进行的；有条理、有系统的。它描述人或程序，而不描述一条路线。

entries.definition: in an orderly, step-by-step way. It answers 'how', while method answers 'by what route'.
entries.definitionCN: 有条理地、一步一步地。它回答“怎样做”，而 method 回答“走哪条路”。

entries.definition: to reduce something to order or system. The verb turns the noun into an action; it is rare outside formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物整理成秩序或体系。这个动词把名词变成动作；在正式写作之外很少见。

entries.definition: a way of dealing with a problem or subject, often including the attitude behind it. It is broader and softer than method, which implies explicit steps.
entries.definitionCN: 处理问题或课题的方式，常包含背后的态度。它比 method 更宽、更软，而 method 暗示明确的步骤。

entries.definition: a particular way of carrying out a single task, especially one requiring skill. Techniques are the small parts inside a method.
entries.definitionCN: 完成单项任务的具体方式，尤指需要技巧的那种。technique 是 method 内部的一个个小零件。

entries.definition: a thing or resource used to achieve an end. Means answers 'with what'; method answers 'in what order'.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目的而使用的东西或资源。means 回答“用什么”，method 回答“按什么顺序”。

entries.definition: an established or official sequence of steps. It is more bureaucratic than method and often written down by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 既定的或官方的步骤顺序。它比 method 更带行政色彩，常由某个权威写下来。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road', the Latin borrowing methodus, and the family methodical, methodology, methodize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”、拉丁语借词 methodus，以及 methodical、methodology、methodize 词族。

normal.en: hodos means 'road'. A method is literally 'a following after on a road': meta plus hodos.
normal.cn: hodos 意为“路”。method 字面上就是“沿路跟随”：meta 加 hodos。

normal.en: In method, meta- does not mean 'beyond' or 'after' as it does in modern English; it means 'in pursuit of'. The Greek preposition is about chasing, not about position.
normal.cn: 在 method 里，meta- 不像现代英语那样表示“超越”或“之后”，而是“追寻”。这个希腊语介词讲的是追赶，不是位置。

normal.en: Methodology is not a fancy word for method: it is the study of methods, or the whole set of them used in a field.
normal.cn: methodology 不是 method 的高级说法：它是对方法的研究，或某一领域所使用的整套方法。

normal.en: Methodical describes the person who always walks on a path; method names the path itself.
normal.cn: methodical 描述那个总沿着路走的人；method 命名的是那条路本身。

normal.en: Medical looks similar but is Latin medicus 'physician'. One word has a road in it, the other has a doctor.
normal.cn: medical 看着像，其实是拉丁语 medicus“医生”。一个词里装着一条路，另一个词里装着一位医生。

abstract.en: Picture grass in a field. One path is visible because many feet chose the same line; that line is a method.
abstract.cn: 想象一片草地。有一条路看得见，是因为许多脚选择了同一条线；那条线就是 method。

abstract.en: A path can be walked by one person or written down for a school. The moment it is written down, method becomes methodology.
abstract.cn: 一条路可以由一个人走，也可以写下来给一个学派。写下来的那一刻，method 就变成了 methodology。

abstract.en: Method is the order of steps, not the tool in your hand. A hammer is a means; how you swing it is a technique; the sequence is the method.
abstract.cn: method 是步骤的顺序，不是你手里的工具。锤子是 means；怎么挥是 technique；先后次序才是 method。

examples.en: No method will save a study that was badly designed in the first place.
examples.cn: 如果一项研究一开始就设计得很糟，任何方法都救不了它。

examples.en: She works without method, yet somehow finishes before everyone else.
examples.cn: 她做事毫无章法，却总能比别人先做完。

examples.en: The two laboratories use different methods and keep getting different numbers.
examples.cn: 两个实验室用不同的方法，得到的数字也一直不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: “卖瑟德”——卖瑟德把一条踩出来的小路画在纸上，卖给后来的人照着走 → method 方法、办法（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自希腊语 methodos“追寻、探究”，由 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”构成，核心是“沿着一条路追到目标”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of method, all from one image: a line worn into the grass by feet that wanted the same destination. It can be one path, the habit of taking paths, or the written map of them.
sensesIntro.cn: method 的九个义项都来自同一幅画面：一条被想抵达同一目标的脚踩出来的草径。它可以是某一条路、走路的习惯，或被写下来的路线图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path worn into grass, pointing at a destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被踩进草地的小路，指向某个目的地。

branches.en: THE PATH: the oldest senses name a procedure, first for curing disease, then for anything at all.
branches.cn: 路：最老的义项命名一套程序，先用于治病，后用于任何事。

branches.en: THE HABIT: orderliness is walking on a path by choice, and the idiom says a path may hide inside apparent chaos.
branches.cn: 习惯：条理是有意识地沿路走；那条习语则说，混乱里也可能藏着一条路。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: written rules turn a path into a teachable system, and science inherits the oldest 'inquiry' sense.
branches.cn: 体系：写下来的规则把路变成可教的体系，而科学继承的是最古老的“探究”义。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: teaching and acting give the path a proper name, and philosophy makes the pursuit itself a rule.
branches.cn: 学派：教学与表演给这条路一个专名，哲学则把追寻本身变成规则。

branches.en: THE CODE: in software the object still knows a fixed route to take when called.
branches.cn: 代码：在软件里，对象被调用时仍知道该走哪条固定路线。

intro.en: Method is a Greek compound borrowed whole: meta- plus hodos 'road'. English adds -ical, -ically, -ology, -ologist and -ize, while the same hodos builds episode, period and Exodus.
intro.cn: method 是整体借入的希腊语复合词：meta- 加 hodos“路”。英语加上 -ical、-ically、-ology、-ologist、-ize，而同一个 hodos 还构成 episode、period、Exodus。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek word unchanged as methodus 'way of teaching or going', and Late Latin methodicus came from Greek methodikos. Latin had its own word for 'way', modus, but method did not come from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语原样吸收希腊词作 methodus“教学或行走之道”，晚期拉丁语 methodicus 来自希腊语 methodikos。拉丁语自己表示“方式”的词是 modus，但 method 并非来自它。

items.meaning: a following after on a road; a way of doing something
items.meaningCN: 沿路追寻；做某事的方法（meta- 追寻 + hodos 路）
items.example: They tried every method and failed with each.
items.exampleCN: 他们试了每一种方法，每一种都失败了。

items.meaningCN: 按方法进行的；有条理的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: His methodical notes filled four notebooks.
items.exampleCN: 他条理分明的笔记写满了四个本子。

items.meaningCN: 有条理地；一步一步地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 她逐个抽屉有条理地检查。

items.meaning: the study of methods; a set of methods used in a field
items.meaningCN: 方法论；一套研究方法（-ology 表学问）
items.example: The paper was rejected for its weak methodology.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文因方法论薄弱而被拒。

items.example: The two studies differ on methodological grounds.
items.exampleCN: 这两项研究在方法上存在分歧。

items.meaning: a specialist in methods of research
items.example: A methodologist was added to the review panel.
items.exampleCN: 评审组里增加了一位方法论专家。

items.meaning: to arrange according to a system
items.meaningCN: 使有条理；使系统化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: He methodized the archive over one winter.
items.exampleCN: 他用一个冬天把档案整理成体系。

items.meaning: a member of the Protestant denomination founded at Oxford in 1729
items.meaningCN: 卫理公会教徒（-ist 表追随者，源于其讲究方法的修行方式）
items.example: The Methodist chapel still stands on the corner.
items.exampleCN: 卫理公会礼拜堂仍立在街角。

items.structure: epi- (besides) + eisodos (a coming in, from hodos 'way')
items.meaning: an incident or instalment inserted into a larger whole
items.meaningCN: 插曲；（系列中的）一集（epi- 另外 + eisodos 进入，含 hodos 路）
items.exampleCN: 最后一集什么也没解答。

items.meaning: a going round; a length of time
items.meaningCN: 周期；一段时间（peri- 环绕 + hodos 路，即“绕一圈”）
items.example: The period lasted almost a century.
items.exampleCN: 这一时期持续了将近一个世纪。

items.meaning: a going out; a mass departure
items.meaningCN: 出走；大批离去（ex- 向外 + hodos 路）
items.example: The drought set off an exodus from the villages.
items.exampleCN: 旱灾引发了村庄的大批出走。

items.meaning: a performance technique that draws on the actor's own experience
items.meaningCN: 方法派表演（以体系命名的表演技术）
items.example: Method acting changed how American films were shot.
items.exampleCN: 方法派表演改变了美国电影的拍摄方式。

definition_zh: 公制的；度量的；格律的；度量指标
definition_en: based on the metric system; also relating to measurement or to poetic metre, and as a noun a measure used to judge performance
core_image: 一把带刻度的尺，把长度拆成一个个可以比较的数字
scene: 实验室的白板上列着两套单位，年轻的研究员把英制数字逐个换算成公制。The intern turned every figure on the board into metric units.
sceneCN: 这里是「公制的」（第 1 个义项：使用公制单位计量）；句意为实习生把白板上的每个数字都换成了公制单位。图中可辨识物件：白板、粉笔、写满数字的表格。

pos.zh: 公制的；度量的；格律的
度量指标

derivatives.zh: 由 metric 加 -al 构成，义为「格律的；度量的」
由 metric 加 -ation 构成，义为「改用公制」
由 metrical 加 -ly 构成，义为「按公制地；按格律地」

senses.title: Relating to the metric system
senses.definition: using or based on the metric system, in which units such as the metre and the kilogram are used
senses.definitionCN: 使用或基于公制的，即以米、千克等单位计量
senses.example: The label lists the weight in metric units.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上用公制单位标注重量。
senses.why: The Greek root metron meant a measure, and after the French reform the adjective was attached to the system built on the metre, so metric labels anything counted in those units.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 metron 意为「尺度」，法国公制改革之后这个形容词被贴到以米为基础的那套单位上，凡是按这套单位计量的东西都叫 metric。

senses.title: A measurement used to judge performance
senses.definition: a measurement used to judge performance or progress, most often in the plural form metrics
senses.definitionCN: 用来衡量表现或进展的测量值，最常用复数形式 metrics
senses.example: The team reviews three metrics every Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每周一复盘三项指标。
senses.why: If metron is any measure, then a single number taken from a process is also a metron, and business English turned that into the countable metrics of a dashboard.
senses.whyCN: 既然 metron 泛指任何一种度量，那么从流程里取出一个数字也是一种度量，商业英语便把它变成仪表盘上可数的 metrics。

senses.title: Of measurement in general
senses.definition: concerned with measuring distance, size or quantity rather than with the units of one particular system
senses.definitionCN: 与距离、大小或数量的测量有关，而不是特指某一套单位
senses.example: In a metric space, distance is defined by a rule rather than by a ruler.
senses.exampleCN: 在度量空间里，距离由一条规则定义，而不是用尺子量出。
senses.why: Mathematics kept the oldest sense of metron as sheer measure, so metric can describe any structure that allows a distance to be assigned, with no metres or inches involved.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留了 metron 最古老的「度量」本义，因此 metric 可以描述任何一种能给出距离的结构，与米或英寸都无关。

senses.title: Of poetic metre
senses.definition: relating to metre, the patterned rhythm of stressed and unstressed syllables in verse
senses.definitionCN: 与格律有关的，即诗句中轻重音节形成的节奏模式
senses.example: The critic counted the metric feet in each line.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者数了每一行里的格律音步。
senses.why: Greek metrikos described verse measured out in feet, and the same adjective survived in literary criticism long after it had been applied to weights and lengths.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 metrikos 本指按音步「量」出来的诗句，这个形容词在文学批评里一直保留，后来才被用到重量与长度上。

intro.en: Metric comes from a Greek word for measure, reached English through Latin and French, and split between the sense of a system of units and the sense of a numbered measure.
intro.cn: metric 出自希腊语中表示「度量」的词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，并在「单位体系」与「可计量的数值」两个方向上都站稳了脚。

items.en: Metron was any measure or unit of length, and it also named the unit of rhythm in verse.
items.cn: metron 泛指任何尺度或长度单位，也指诗句中节奏的单位。

items.en: The adjective metrikos meant of measure and was used especially for the measured rhythm of poetry.
items.cn: 形容词 metrikos 意为「关于度量的」，尤用于诗句中被量出的节奏。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as metricus, keeping the literary and measuring senses together.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词写作 metricus，把文学与度量两层意思一并保留。

items.en: During the French reform of weights and measures, the word was fixed to the system based on the metre, and the phrase système métrique spread across Europe.
items.cn: 在法国度量衡改革中，这个词被固定到以米为基础的体系上，système métrique 这一说法传遍欧洲。

items.en: English took metric in the nineteenth century for the system of units, then reused it for any number a business tracks and for the older sense of verse rhythm.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入 metric 指单位体系，随后又用它指企业追踪的任何数值，并保留了诗律的旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek measure root through metre, geometry and the derived adjective; the near-meaning group collects words for measuring and for standards of comparison.
note.cn: 形近组顺着希腊语「度量」词根，收 metre、geometry 与派生形容词；近义组收表示测量与比较标准的词。

entries.definition: The base unit of length in the metric system.
entries.definitionCN: 公制中长度的基本单位。

entries.definition: The American spelling of metre; also a device that measures.
entries.definitionCN: metre 的美式拼写；也指计量仪表。

entries.definition: Relating to poetic metre or to measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 与诗律或度量有关的。

entries.definition: The mathematics of shapes and distances, named from measuring the earth.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形状与距离的数学，名字来自「测量土地」。

entries.definition: The act or result of finding a size or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 测量行为或测量所得的结果。

entries.definition: A fixed amount used as a standard for measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 作为计量标准的固定量。

entries.definition: An instrument or standard used for measuring something.
entries.definitionCN: 测量用的仪器或标准。

entries.definition: A standard point of reference for judging performance.
entries.definitionCN: 评判表现所用的参照标准。

normalIntro.en: One Greek word for measure runs through units, geometry and verse, so the family looks scattered but keeps a single idea.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「度量」的希腊词贯穿单位、几何与诗句，所以这一族看着分散，内核却只有一个。

normal.en: Metron is Greek for a measure, and metre is the measure the metric system starts from.
normal.cn: metron 是希腊语中的「尺度」，metre 正是公制起步的那把尺。

normal.en: Metric as an adjective belongs to the system, which is why metric system and metric unit appear as fixed pairs.
normal.cn: 作形容词的 metric 依附于这套体系，所以 metric system 与 metric unit 是固定搭配。

normal.en: Metrics, the plural noun, turns one measurement into the set of numbers a dashboard watches.
normal.cn: 复数名词 metrics 把一次测量变成仪表盘上盯着的一组数字。

normal.en: Geometry ends in the same Greek word, so its name literally means measuring the land.
normal.cn: geometry 的词尾是同一个希腊词，名字字面上就是「测量土地」。

normal.en: Metrical keeps the verse sense, because Greek metre also counted the feet of a line.
normal.cn: metrical 保留了诗句的义项，因为希腊语的 metre 也用来数一行诗的音步。

abstract.en: A ruler and a dashboard do the same thing: they turn the world into numbers someone can compare.
abstract.cn: 尺子和仪表盘做的是同一件事：把世界变成可以互相比较的数字。

abstract.en: The word sits between a poem and a machine, measuring both a line of verse and a sack of grain.
abstract.cn: 这个词站在诗与机器之间，既量一行诗，也称一袋粮食。

abstract.en: Choosing what to count is choosing what matters, so a metric is never a neutral number.
abstract.cn: 决定数什么，就是决定在意什么，所以指标从来不是中立的数字。

examples.en: The form asks for your height in metric units.
examples.cn: 表格要求用公制单位填写身高。

examples.en: We track two metrics: response time and error rate.
examples.cn: 我们跟踪两项指标：响应时间和错误率。

examples.en: The poet kept a strict metric pattern in every line.
examples.cn: 这位诗人在每一行都保持严格的格律。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米特里克」——头一个字就是米，公制从米量起；记住 metric 是公制的，也指度量指标。

root: 希腊语 metron（尺度）派生 metrikos（关于度量的），经晚期拉丁语 metricus 与法语 métrique 进入英语；同族词包括 metre 与 geometry。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of measuring; the senses divide into a system of units, a countable number on a dashboard, measurement in general, and the measured rhythm of verse.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「度量」这个动作；义项分到单位体系、仪表盘上的可数数值、一般意义的测量，以及被量出节奏的诗句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler with fine marks, turning length into numbers that can be compared.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刻着细密刻度的尺，把长度变成可以互相比较的数字。

branches.en: a cookbook printing grams beside ounces
branches.cn: 食谱上把克与盎司并排印出

branches.en: a dashboard with three numbers on it
branches.cn: 仪表盘上只挂着三个数字

branches.en: a map where distance comes from a rule, not a ruler
branches.cn: 地图上的距离由规则给出，而不是用尺量

branches.en: a line of verse scanned for its beat
branches.cn: 一行诗被数出它的节拍

branches.en: the same act of measuring, once in units and once in numbers
branches.cn: 同一个测量动作，一次落在单位上，一次落在数字上

intro.en: Greek measure and its adjective supply the stem, and English suffixes and the geometry compound carry the family in several directions.
intro.cn: 希腊语的「度量」名词与形容词提供词干，再由英语后缀与 geometry 这个复合词把词族引向几个方向。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 大都市；首要城市；特大城市的中心；文化或经济中心；宗主国城市；大主教座城市
definition_en: a very large and important city, especially one that is the centre of a region
core_image: 从高处看，高架桥一层层叠起，灯光一直铺到看不见的地平线，城市没有明显的边
scene: 从观景台看下去，高架桥层层叠叠，灯光一直铺到看不见的地平线。The metropolis keeps moving long after midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 metropolis 指「规模极大、并作为区域中心的大城市」（第 1 个义项：首要大城市）；句意为这座大都市在午夜之后仍不停歇。可辨识物件：观景台、高架桥、车灯、地平线。

pos.zh: 大都市；首要城市（可数，复数 metropolises）

derivatives.zh: metropolis 去掉词尾 -is 加拉丁 -itan（形容词后缀）→ 由「母城」偏移为「属于大都市的」
希腊 mētropolis 经法语 métropole → 偏移为「相对殖民地的宗主国本土」
metropolitan 的截短形式 → 偏移为「大都市的地铁系统」
mega-（巨大）+ polis（城）→ 偏移为「连成一片的巨型城市带」
necro-（死者）+ polis（城）→ 偏移为「墓城、大型墓地」
metropolitan + -ism（名词后缀）→ 偏移为「以大都市为中心的生活方式与心态」

senses.title: A great city
senses.definition: a city of great size and importance, usually the leading city of a country or region
senses.definitionCN: 规模与重要性都很高、通常是某国或某地区首位城市的城市
senses.example: The metropolis keeps moving long after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大都市在午夜之后仍不停歇。
senses.why: Greek mētēr 'mother' plus polis 'city' named the mother city of a colony, and size and centrality grew out of that role.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 mētēr「母亲」加 polis「城」原指殖民地的母城，规模与中心地位都从这个角色生长出来。

senses.title: A city by sheer size
senses.titleCN: 按人口规模而言的特大城市
senses.definition: a city defined chiefly by the number of people packed into it
senses.definitionCN: 主要以聚居于其中的人口数量来界定的大城
senses.example: By population alone, the delta holds three metropolises.
senses.exampleCN: 仅按人口计算，这个三角洲就有三座特大城市。
senses.why: once the word lost its colonial meaning, sheer scale was enough to earn it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词失去殖民义，单凭规模就足以取得它。

senses.title: A regional hub
senses.definition: the city through which a region's transport, trade and administration run
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区的交通、贸易与行政所经的中心城市
senses.example: Every rail line in the province ends at the metropolis.
senses.exampleCN: 全省每一条铁路都终点于这座中心城市。
senses.why: being a mother city means other places depend on you, and dependence is what makes a hub.
senses.whyCN: 作为母城意味着别的地方依赖你，而依赖正是枢纽之所以为枢纽。

senses.title: An imperial mother city
senses.definition: in colonial usage, the home city or country ruling over a dependent territory
senses.definitionCN: 在殖民用法中，统治附属地的本土城市或本国
senses.example: The colony shipped its raw material to the metropolis.
senses.exampleCN: 殖民地把它原料运往宗主国城市。
senses.why: this is the original sense restored: the mother city that a settlement looked back to.
senses.whyCN: 这是原义的回返：移居地回头仰望的那座母城。

senses.title: A cultural and economic centre
senses.definition: a city that concentrates a country's publishing, finance, fashion or education
senses.definitionCN: 集中一国出版、金融、时尚或教育的城市
senses.example: The metropolis sets the style that the provinces copy.
senses.exampleCN: 这座都市定下风格，外地再模仿。
senses.why: centrality in institutions followed centrality in politics, and the word widened to any dominant centre.
senses.whyCN: 机构上的中心性跟着政治上的中心性而来，这个词便扩展到任何占主导的中心。

senses.title: An archbishop's seat
senses.titleCN: 大主教座所在城市（教会义）
senses.definition: the see of a metropolitan bishop, who oversees the bishops of a province
senses.definitionCN: 大主教座所在之地，该主教管辖一教省的诸主教
senses.example: The old metropolis still holds the cathedral and the archives.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古老的座城仍保有主教座堂与档案。
senses.why: the church kept the administrative sense of the mother city long after empires had gone.
senses.whyCN: 帝国消失很久之后，教会仍保留着「母城」的行政义。

senses.title: A city in fiction
senses.titleCN: 虚构作品中的巨型城市
senses.definition: an imagined city of enormous scale used as a setting or a character
senses.definitionCN: 作为背景或角色使用的、规模巨大的想象城市
senses.example: The novel's metropolis has no edges, only weather.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里的那座巨型城市没有边界，只有天气。
senses.why: fiction pushes the defining trait, sheer size, until the city becomes a condition rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 虚构把它的核心特征——纯粹的规模——推到极致，直到城市成为一种处境而不是一个地点。

senses.title: A figurative centre
senses.definition: the acknowledged centre of a activity, used figuratively of a place or institution
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动公认的中心，用于地点或机构的比喻说法
senses.example: That laboratory is the metropolis of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 那间实验室是该领域的中心。
senses.why: if a metropolis is where everything converges, any converging point can be called one.
senses.whyCN: 如果大都市是一切汇聚之处，那么任何汇聚点都可以被称为大都市。

intro.en: Metropolis is Greek mētēr 'mother' plus polis 'city', naming the mother city of a colony; it reached English through Late Latin and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: metropolis 由希腊 mētēr「母亲」加 polis「城」构成，指殖民地的母城；它经晚期拉丁与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mētēr meant 'mother'; its Indo-European origin is generally thought to be the widespread *mater- root, though the Greek form itself is attested, not reconstructed.
items.cn: mētēr 意为「母亲」；一般认为其印欧来源是广泛分布的 *mater- 词根，不过希腊语形式本身有书证，并非重构。

items.en: Polis meant 'city, citizen-body'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and no single Indo-European source has been accepted.
items.cn: polis 意为「城邦、公民群体」。其更早来源不确定，也没有公认的单一印欧语来源。

items.en: Mētropolis named the mother city of a colony, the place from which settlers came and to which the settlement remained tied.
items.cn: mētropolis 指殖民地的母城，即移居者来处、也是移居地仍与之相连的地方。

items.en: Late Latin used metropolis as a Greek loanword, chiefly in church administration for a bishop's seat.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁把 metropolis 作为希腊借词使用，主要用于教会行政，指主教座所在之城。

items.en: French métropole carried the word into modern European languages, where it widened from mother city to any great city.
items.cn: 法语 métropole 把这个词带入近代欧洲诸语言，其义从母城扩展为任何大城。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of polis before Greek is unsettled, and no attested earlier form exists, so any proposed pre-Greek root is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定：polis 在希腊语之前的来源无定论，也没有有书证的更早形式，因此任何提出的希腊语之前词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the polis family and its look-alikes; group two holds the terms for very large urban units.
note.cn: 第一组是 polis 词族及其形近词；第二组是表示超大城市场域的术语。

entries.definition: Relating to a metropolis or its whole region; it describes, while metropolis names the city.
entries.definitionCN: 与大都市或其整个区域相关；它作描述，而 metropolis 指城市本身。

entries.definition: The home territory of a colonial power, as seen from the colony; it is the political half of the older word.
entries.definitionCN: 从殖民地视角看的宗主国本土；它是这个旧词的政治那一半。

entries.definition: A continuous urban region formed when several cities merge; it is larger than one metropolis and not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 由数座城市连并而成的连续城市区域；比单座大都市更大，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A large cemetery, literally a city of the dead; it shares the polis ending but not the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 大型墓地，字面是「死者的城」；它与 metropolis 共享 polis 词尾，意思却不同。

entries.definition: A city of many peoples, literally a world city; the first element is cosmos, not mother.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多民族组成的城市，字面是「世界城」；前一个成分是 cosmos，不是「母亲」。

entries.definition: A city above a fixed population threshold, usually ten million; it is a statistical category, not a historical role.
entries.definitionCN: 人口超过某一固定门槛（通常一千万）的城市；它是统计类别，不是历史角色。

entries.definition: The city where a government sits; a metropolis may or may not be a capital, since the word concerns size and centrality.
entries.definitionCN: 政府所在之城；大都市未必是首都，因为这个词关乎规模与中心性。

entries.definition: A continuous built-up area formed by several towns growing together; it describes the fabric, not the leading city.
entries.definitionCN: 由数个城镇共同生长成的连片建成区；它描述肌理，而非首位城市。

entries.definition: The ordinary term for an urban settlement; metropolis adds scale, centrality and often a historical role.
entries.definitionCN: 城市聚落的一般说法；metropolis 额外带上规模、中心性与常有的历史角色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real Greek elements, the real polis family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的希腊语成分、真实的 polis 词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: mētēr 'mother' + polis 'city': the mother city that a colony looked back to.
normal.cn: mētēr「母亲」+ polis「城」：殖民地回头仰望的母城。

normal.en: The polis family runs metropolis, metropolitan, metropole, megalopolis, necropolis, cosmopolis.
normal.cn: polis 词族包括 metropolis、metropolitan、metropole、megalopolis、necropolis、cosmopolis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: sprawling metropolis, financial metropolis, bustling metropolis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模：不断铺开的大都市、金融大都市、熙攘的大都市。

normal.en: The church kept the administrative sense, so a metropolis can still mean an archbishop's seat.
normal.cn: 教会保留了行政义，因此 metropolis 仍可指大主教座所在之城。

normal.en: Metro is the clipped form of metropolitan, now naming the underground railway.
normal.cn: metro 是 metropolitan 的截短形式，如今指地下铁路。

abstract.en: Picture lights that continue past the last road sign and never quite end.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光越过最后一块路牌还在继续，始终没有真正结束。

abstract.en: Picture a city that is described by weather because its edges cannot be found.
abstract.cn: 想象一座只能用天气来描述的城市，因为找不到它的边缘。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour where every road in the province finally arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一座港口，全省的每条路最后都抵达这里。

examples.en: The metropolis absorbs the labour of four surrounding provinces.
examples.cn: 这座大都市吸纳了周边四个省的劳动力。

examples.en: Long before it was a metropolis, the town was a colonial mother city.
examples.cn: 在这座城成为大都市之前很久，它曾是殖民地的母城。

examples.en: Planners now speak of the whole delta as one metropolis.
examples.cn: 规划者现在把整个三角洲当作一座大都市来谈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「metro（母亲）+ polis（城）」——像母亲一样把周边都拢在怀里的那座城 → 大都市

root: 希腊 mētēr「母亲」+ polis「城」，原指殖民地的母城；经晚期拉丁与法语 métropole 进入英语。polis 更早来源不确定，mētēr 一般认为出自印欧 *mater-。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one role: a mother city, and that role widens into great size, regional centrality, imperial rule, cultural dominance, church administration, fictional vastness and finally any figurative centre.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个角色展开：母城，而这个角色依次扩展为巨大规模、区域中心、宗主统治、文化主导、教会管辖、虚构的浩大，最后是任何比喻意义上的中心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a city that other places point toward, as a child points toward a mother.
core.cn: 核心意象：别的地方都朝向它的一座城，像一个孩子朝向母亲。

branches.en: THE MOTHER CITY AND ITS SCALE: the original role, then sheer size as a sufficient claim to the name.
branches.cn: 母城与规模：先是原初角色，随后单凭规模就足以取得这个名字。

branches.en: THE HUB: other places depend on it for transport, trade and administration.
branches.cn: 枢纽：别的地方在交通、贸易与行政上依赖它。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF AUTHORITY: the colonial mother country and the archbishop's seat both rule from a centre.
branches.cn: 两种权威：殖民地母国与大主教座城都从一个中心施行管辖。

branches.en: CULTURAL DOMINANCE: institutions concentrate there, and the provinces copy its style.
branches.cn: 文化主导：机构集中于此，外地模仿它的风格。

branches.en: THE WORD LOOSENED: fiction takes the vastness as a condition, and ordinary speech takes the centre as a metaphor.
branches.cn: 词的松动：虚构把它的大当作一种处境，日常语言则把它的中心当作比喻。

intro.en: Metropolis is a Greek compound of two very productive elements, and the second of them builds a whole family of city words.
intro.cn: metropolis 是由两个构词力极强的希腊成分组成的复合词，其中后一个成分建起了一整族「城」的词。

latinIntro.en: There is no inherited Latin family: metropolis entered Latin only as a Greek loanword, mainly in church usage, so no genuine Latin cognate exists.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语固有词族：metropolis 只作为希腊借词进入拉丁语，且主要用于教会语境，因此不存在真正的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The first element names the parent city.
items.exampleCN: 前一个成分命名的是母城。

items.example: The second element names the city itself.
items.exampleCN: 后一个成分命名的是城市本身。

items.example: The colony sent grain to its metropolis.
The suffix forms metropolitan from metropolis.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 metropolis 变成 metropolitan。

items.example: The coast has become one megalopolis.
items.exampleCN: 这条海岸已连成一片巨型城市带。

items.example: The necropolis lies outside the old walls.
items.exampleCN: 那片墓城位于旧城墙之外。

items.example: The port grew into a cosmopolis.
items.exampleCN: 这座港口长成了一座世界城。

items.example: The metropole imported the colony's rubber.
items.exampleCN: 宗主国进口殖民地的橡胶。

items.example: The metro runs until two in the morning.
Metropolitanism shapes how the capital sees itself.
items.exampleCN: 大都市心态塑造了首都看待自己的方式。

definition_zh: 微生物的；由微生物引起的；与微生物有关的
definition_en: of, relating to, or caused by microbes
core_image: 岩石表面一层黏滑的绿色菌席，在放大镜下由无数微小细胞连成一片
scene: 这里指「微生物的」。 The microbial mat on the rock surface turned the shallow water green.
sceneCN: 这里 microbial 是「微生物的」（第 1 个义项：与微生物相关）；句意：岩石表面的微生物席把浅水染成了绿色。图中可辨识物件：岩石、贴附其上的菌席、被映绿的水面。

pos.zh: 微生物的；由微生物引起的（由名词 microbe 加 -ial 构成，范围比 bacterial 更宽）

derivatives.zh: 微生物（尤指致病的微小生物）
微生物（复数）
微生物的（罕用变体）
以微生物方式地

senses.title: Of Microbes in General
senses.titleCN: 微生物的：与微生物这一类相关
senses.definition: relating to microbes as a broad class of small life
senses.definitionCN: 与作为一大类微小生命的微生物有关的
senses.example: Microbial life exists in every handful of garden soil.
senses.exampleCN: 每一把园土里都有微生物生命。
senses.why: Microbial is built on microbe, a popular nineteenth-century word for small life. The suffix -ial marks relation, so the adjective is wider than bacterial and can cover fungi and protists as well.
senses.whyCN: microbial 建立在 microbe 上，那是十九世纪指微小生命的通俗词；后缀 -ial 表示关联，因此这个形容词比 bacterial 更宽，也能涵盖真菌与原生生物。

senses.title: Microbial Life
senses.titleCN: 微生物生命：作为生命形态本身
senses.definition: the living activity of microbes taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把微生物作为整体来看的生命活动
senses.example: Microbial life in the vent thrives without sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 热泉喷口处的微生物生命不依赖阳光而繁盛。
senses.why: Here the adjective modifies life itself, not a process or a disease. The phrase treats microbes as a form of life with its own chemistry, such as chemosynthesis.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词修饰的是「生命」本身，而不是某个过程或疾病；该短语把微生物视为一种有自身化学机制（如化能合成）的生命形态。

senses.title: A Microbial Community
senses.titleCN: 微生物群落的：共同生活的集合
senses.definition: relating to a community or assemblage of microbes
senses.definitionCN: 与微生物群落或集合体有关的
senses.example: The microbial community in the gut shifted after the antibiotic.
senses.exampleCN: 使用抗生素后，肠道中的微生物群落发生了变化。
senses.why: A community is more than many cells; it is a set of populations that interact. The adjective marks that ecological level, which is why microbial community and microbiome are so frequent.
senses.whyCN: 群落不只是许多细胞，而是相互作用的种群集合；这个形容词标出的是生态层次，因此 microbial community 与 microbiome 如此常用。

senses.title: Microbial Growth
senses.titleCN: 微生物生长的：数量增加的过程
senses.definition: relating to the increase of microbial populations
senses.definitionCN: 与微生物种群数量增加有关的
senses.example: Microbial growth in the tank was measured every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 罐中的微生物生长每小时测量一次。
senses.why: Growth here is population growth, not the enlargement of one body. The adjective attaches the process to the microbial level, as bacterial growth does for one kind of microbe.
senses.whyCN: 这里的生长是种群增长，而不是单个身体变大；这个形容词把过程固定在微生物层次，正如 bacterial growth 固定于细菌这一类。

senses.title: Microbial Infection
senses.titleCN: 微生物感染的：由微生物侵入引起
senses.definition: caused by microbes entering a host
senses.definitionCN: 由微生物侵入宿主引起的
senses.example: The burns unit screened every patient for microbial infection.
senses.exampleCN: 烧伤病房对每位病人进行微生物感染筛查。
senses.why: In clinical use the adjective can stand in for a cause, like bacterial but broader. The speaker may not yet know which microbe is responsible, so the general term is preferred.
senses.whyCN: 在临床用法中，这个形容词可以像 bacterial 一样表示病因，但范围更宽；说话人可能还不知道是哪种微生物，因此宁用泛称。

senses.title: Microbial Technology
senses.titleCN: 微生物技术的：把微生物当作工具
senses.definition: relating to the use of microbes in technology or industry
senses.definitionCN: 与在技术或工业中利用微生物有关的
senses.example: The microbial fuel cell produced current from waste water.
senses.exampleCN: 微生物燃料电池用废水产生了电流。
senses.why: Here microbes are components of an engineered system. The adjective moves from biology to engineering: the organism is valued for a function it can be made to perform.
senses.whyCN: 这里微生物是工程系统的部件；这个形容词从生物学转向工程学：生物体因其可被安排执行的功能而受重视。

senses.title: Microbial Decomposition
senses.titleCN: 微生物分解的：物质循环中的分解
senses.definition: relating to the breakdown of matter by microbes
senses.definitionCN: 与微生物分解物质有关的
senses.example: Microbial decomposition returned the carbon to the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 微生物分解把碳归还给土壤。
senses.why: Decomposition is a service performed by microbes in every ecosystem. The adjective names the agent of the process, which is why it often appears in ecology and waste treatment.
senses.whyCN: 分解是微生物在每个生态系统中提供的服务；这个形容词命名过程的执行者，因此常出现在生态学与废物处理语境中。

senses.title: Microbial Contamination
senses.titleCN: 微生物污染的：产品或环境被沾染
senses.definition: relating to contamination by microbes
senses.definitionCN: 与微生物造成的污染有关的
senses.example: Microbial contamination closed the bottling line for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 微生物污染使灌装线停工一周。
senses.why: Contamination names the entry of unwanted microbes into a product or a place. The adjective identifies the kind of unwanted life, not the process by which it got in.
senses.whyCN: 污染指不需要的微生物进入产品或场所；这个形容词指明的是不受欢迎的生命种类，而不是它们进入的方式。

intro.en: Microbial is the adjective of microbe, a French coinage of 1878 that was itself built from two Greek elements. Its birth date is known, but its second element was chosen in a way that Greek would not have allowed.
intro.cn: microbial 是 microbe 的形容词，microbe 是 1878 年法语造出的词，本身由两个希腊成分构成。它的生日已知，但第二个成分的选择方式在希腊语里其实并不成立。

items.en: Greek mikros, Attic for smikros, meant 'small'. Its Latinized form micro- became the scientific prefix for the very small. Beekes suggests the Greek word may be Pre-Greek, so its deeper source is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 mikros（阿提卡形式 smikros）意为「小」，其拉丁化形式 micro- 成为表示「极小」的科学前缀。Beekes 认为这个希腊词可能来自前希腊语底层，因此更深来源不确定。

items.en: Greek bios meant 'life, course of life, lifetime', as opposed to zōē, 'animal life'. It supplies the second element of many modern compounds through the combining form bio-.
items.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为「生命、生命历程、寿命」，与表示动物生命的 zōē 相对；它通过组合形式 bio- 为许多现代复合词提供第二成分。

items.en: French microbe was coined in 1878 by the surgeon Charles Sédillot. Etymonline, quoting Weekley, calls it 'badly coined', because in Greek the compound would mean 'short-lived' rather than 'small living thing'. The intended meaning won anyway.
items.cn: 法语 microbe 由外科医生夏尔·塞迪约于 1878 年创制。etymonline 引用 Weekley 的说法称其「造得不好」，因为在希腊语中这个复合词会表示「短命的」，而不是「微小的生物」。但意图中的意义最终胜出。

items.en: Microbial is recorded from 1879, from Modern Latin microbion, the Latinized form of microbe, plus the adjective ending -al. The adjective therefore entered English one year after the noun.
items.cn: microbial 记录于 1879 年，由 microbe 的拉丁化形式现代拉丁 microbion 加形容词词尾 -al 构成；因此形容词比名词晚一年进入英语。

items.en: Microbe was coined as a popular word for disease-causing small life; microorganism, from 1855, is the neutral scientific term. Microbial inherits the popular word's breadth and its medical flavour.
items.cn: microbe 创制时是「致病微小生命」的通俗词，而 1855 年出现的 microorganism 是中性的科学术语。microbial 继承了通俗词的宽泛范围与医学色彩。

items.en: Since the 2000s microbial has appeared in microbial ecology, microbial genetics and microbiome research. In these names it marks a level of biological organisation rather than a single organism.
items.cn: 自本世纪以来，microbial 出现在微生物生态学、微生物遗传学与微生物组研究中；在这些名称里，它标出的是一个生物组织层次，而不是单个生物体。

note.en: The first group holds adjectives and nouns built on the microbe stem. The second group holds overlapping terms whose scope or register differs.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 microbe 词干上的形容词与名词；第二组是范围或语体不同的重叠词。

entries.definition: An older and rarer synonym of microbial, formed with -ic instead of -ial. It appears mainly in nineteenth- and early twentieth-century writing.
entries.definitionCN: microbial 的旧式罕用同义词，用 -ic 而非 -ial 构成；主要见于十九世纪与二十世纪初的文字。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning 'by or with microbes'. It is technical and uncommon outside laboratory writing.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「借微生物作用地」；属于技术用语，实验室文字之外少见。

entries.definition: The study of microbes. The ending -logy marks a field, so it cannot substitute for the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 研究微生物的学科；词尾 -logy 表示领域，不能代替形容词使用。

entries.definition: Of bacteria only. It is the right word when the group is known to be bacterial, and microbial is the right word when fungi or protists may be involved.
entries.definitionCN: 只指细菌的；当已知是细菌时用 bacterial，当可能涉及真菌或原生生物时用 microbial。

entries.definition: Relating to microbiology as a discipline or to its methods, as in microbiological testing. It points to the science, not directly to the organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 与微生物学这一学科或其方法有关的，如微生物学检测；它指向学科，而不是直接指向生物体。

entries.definition: Disease-causing. It says nothing about size or kingdom, and many microbes are not pathogenic.
entries.definitionCN: 指致病的；不涉及大小或生物界，而许多微生物并不致病。

entries.tag: adjective of seeds or early growth
entries.definition: Relating to a germ or seed, or to an early stage of development. It is not a synonym of microbial despite the everyday sense of germ.
entries.definitionCN: 指胚芽、种子或发育早期的；尽管 germ 有「病菌」的日常义，germinal 并不是 microbial 的同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: microbe + -ial: 'having to do with microbes', broader than bacterial.
normal.cn: microbe + -ial：意为「与微生物有关」，范围比 bacterial 更宽。

normal.en: micro- is 'small', bios is 'life'; the compound was meant to say 'small life'.
normal.cn: micro- 是「小」，bios 是「生命」；这个复合词本意是说「微小的生命」。

normal.en: The noun arrived in 1878 and the adjective in 1879, so the pair is almost the same age.
normal.cn: 名词 1878 年出现，形容词 1879 年出现，两者几乎同龄。

normal.en: The family runs microbe, microbes, microbial, microbic, microbially, microbiology and microbiome.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 microbe、microbes、microbial、microbic、microbially、microbiology、microbiome。

normal.en: Use microbial when the kind is unknown or mixed; use bacterial when only bacteria are meant.
normal.cn: 种类未知或混杂时用 microbial；只指细菌时用 bacterial。

abstract.en: Picture a green skin over a wet rock, made of cells too small to name one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象湿岩石上的一层绿皮，由小到无法逐个命名的细胞构成。

abstract.en: Picture a city whose citizens are invisible but whose work keeps the streets clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，市民看不见，而他们的工作让街道保持清洁。

abstract.en: Picture a power station run by creatures you need a lens to meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由必须借助镜片才能见到的生物运转的电站。

examples.en: Microbial activity made the sealed jar swell with gas.
examples.cn: 微生物活动使密封罐因气体而鼓起。

examples.en: The microbial community on the skin protects against some invaders.
examples.cn: 皮肤上的微生物群落能抵御某些入侵者。

examples.en: Microbial contamination was found in three of the sampled bottles.
examples.cn: 抽样检测的瓶子中有三瓶发现了微生物污染。

dict_mnemonic.text: microbe（微生物）+ -ial（与……有关的）→ 与微生物有关的 → microbial 微生物的

root: 希腊 mikros「小」→ 拉丁化 micro- + 希腊 bios「生命」→ 法语 microbe（1878 年塞迪约创制）→ 现代拉丁 microbion → 英语 microbial（microbion + -al，1879）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses attach the adjective to eight objects: the class, life itself, a community, a population, an infection, a technology, a decomposition and a contamination.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个形容词接到八个对象上：类别、生命本身、群落、种群、感染、技术、分解与污染。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slippery green mat over wet rock, made of countless invisible cells.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿岩石上的一层滑绿菌席，由无数看不见的细胞构成。

branches.en: THE CLASS AND LIFE: the broadest relation, then the same adjective applied to life as a form.
branches.cn: 类别与生命：最宽泛的关联，随后同一形容词落在作为一种形态的生命上。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND QUANTITATIVE: a community is organised, while growth is a population count over time.
branches.cn: 集体与数量：群落是有组织的，生长则是种群随时间的计数。

branches.en: HARM: the adjective can name a cause of disease without naming the species.
branches.cn: 危害：这个形容词可以只命名病因，而不指明物种。

branches.en: WORK: microbes are put to work in fuel cells and in the decomposition that recycles matter.
branches.cn: 工作：微生物被用于燃料电池，也用于使物质循环的分解过程。

branches.en: UNWANTED PRESENCE: contamination is the same life arriving where it is not wanted.
branches.cn: 不受欢迎的存在：污染就是同样的生命来到了不该来的地方。

intro.en: Microbial combines a Greek prefix for smallness, a Greek root for life, and a Latin adjective ending, with a Modern Latin noun in between.
intro.cn: microbial 由表示「微小」的希腊前缀、表示「生命」的希腊词根、中间的现代拉丁名词与拉丁形容词词尾组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin microbion Latinized the French microbe before English added -al. There is no classical Latin etymon for microbe; the Latin-looking shape is a modern scientific construction.
latinIntro.cn: 在现代拉丁语中，microbion 把法语 microbe 拉丁化，随后英语加上 -al。microbe 没有古典拉丁语词源；它看似拉丁的外形只是现代科学构造。

items.meaningCN: 微生物的或由微生物引起的
items.exampleCN: 微生物生长充满了培养皿。

items.example: The microbe was cultured from the wound.
items.exampleCN: 从伤口中培养出了这种微生物。

items.example: Microbes colonise the gut at birth.
items.exampleCN: 微生物在出生时定殖于肠道。

items.example: Old texts speak of microbic disease.
items.exampleCN: 旧文献会说到微生物疾病。

items.example: Microbiology examines both harm and use.
items.exampleCN: 微生物学既研究危害也研究用途。

items.meaningCN: 某一地点的微生物群落
items.example: The oral microbiota differs from the gut's.
items.exampleCN: 口腔微生物区系与肠道的不同。

items.meaning: a microbial community and its genes
items.example: The microbiome was sequenced in full.
items.exampleCN: 该微生物组被完整测序。

senses.title: The Science of Microbes
senses.titleCN: 微生物学：研究微生物的科学
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies microorganisms
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中研究微生物的分支
senses.example: Microbiology asks how a single cell can live, grow and cause disease.
senses.exampleCN: 微生物学追问一个细胞如何生存、生长并致病。
senses.why: The word joins micro-, 'small', biology, 'study of life', and -logy, 'science of'. The core is a discipline, not an organism: it names the organised knowledge about small life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 micro-「小」、biology「生命研究」与 -logy「……学」构成；核心是一门学科，而不是某种生物：它命名的是关于微小生命的系统知识。

senses.title: A Discipline and a Department
senses.titleCN: 学科与院系：作为建制单位
senses.definition: the academic field or the institutional unit that teaches and researches it
senses.definitionCN: 教授与研究该领域的学术建制或单位
senses.example: She joined the microbiology department as a lecturer.
senses.exampleCN: 她以讲师身份加入了微生物学系。
senses.why: A science becomes an institution: it has chairs, degrees, journals and laboratories. The uncountable name can therefore stand for the department that houses the field.
senses.whyCN: 一门科学会变成一种建制：它拥有教席、学位、期刊与实验室；因此这个不可数名词可以代指容纳该领域的院系。

senses.title: Clinical Microbiology
senses.titleCN: 临床微生物学：为诊断服务
senses.definition: the branch that identifies microbes causing human disease
senses.definitionCN: 鉴定引起人类疾病的微生物的分支
senses.example: Clinical microbiology reports the species and its drug sensitivity.
senses.exampleCN: 临床微生物学报告菌种及其药物敏感性。
senses.why: In hospital use the science is narrowed to diagnosis. The adjective clinical marks the setting, and the work is to name the agent and guide treatment.
senses.whyCN: 在医院语境中，这门科学被收窄为诊断用途；形容词 clinical 标出场景，工作内容是命名病原并指导治疗。

senses.title: Food and Industrial Microbiology
senses.titleCN: 食品与工业微生物学：发酵与保质
senses.definition: the branch concerned with fermentation, preservation and industrial use
senses.definitionCN: 研究发酵、防腐与工业应用的微生物学分支
senses.example: Food microbiology keeps cheese cultures pure and spoilage out.
senses.exampleCN: 食品微生物学保持奶酪菌种纯净，并防止腐败。
senses.why: Here the discipline serves production: it manages useful microbes and excludes harmful ones. The same science that studies disease also runs a factory.
senses.whyCN: 这里这门学科为生产服务：管理有益微生物、排除有害微生物；研究疾病的同一门科学，也在经营工厂。

senses.title: Environmental Microbiology
senses.titleCN: 环境微生物学：生境中的微生物
senses.definition: the branch that studies microbes in soil, water and air
senses.definitionCN: 研究土壤、水体与空气中微生物的分支
senses.example: Environmental microbiology traced the oil spill's cleanup to local bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 环境微生物学把漏油的清理归功于本地细菌。
senses.why: The setting shifts from the clinic to the ecosystem. The discipline asks how microbial communities cycle elements and degrade pollutants.
senses.whyCN: 场景从诊室转向生态系统；这门学科研究微生物群落如何循环元素、降解污染物。

senses.title: Laboratory Methods
senses.titleCN: 实验室方法：培养、染色与鉴定
senses.definition: the practical methods of culturing, staining and identifying microbes
senses.definitionCN: 培养、染色与鉴定微生物的实用方法
senses.example: The course begins with the microbiology of streaking a plate.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从平板划线这一微生物学基本操作开始。
senses.why: A science is also a set of hands-on techniques. The name can denote the method side, which is why a laboratory course and a research field share the word.
senses.whyCN: 一门科学也是一套动手技术；这个名称可以指方法层面，因此实验室课程与研究领域共用同一个词。

senses.title: A Course or a Textbook
senses.titleCN: 课程与教材：作为教学科目
senses.definition: a course or textbook that teaches the subject
senses.definitionCN: 教授该科目的课程或教材
senses.example: Microbiology is a second-year course in most biology programmes.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数生物专业中，微生物学是二年级课程。
senses.why: The name of a science can metonymically name its teaching. Students say they are taking microbiology, meaning the course rather than the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 学科名可以通过转喻指它的教学；学生说自己在上微生物学，指的是课程，而不是整个领域。

senses.title: The Microbes of a Sample
senses.titleCN: 样本的微生物组成：转喻用法
senses.definition: the microbial content or profile of a sample or a body site
senses.definitionCN: 某样本或身体部位的微生物组成或图谱
senses.example: The microbiology of the gut changed after the treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗之后，肠道的微生物组成发生了变化。
senses.why: Professional shorthand says the microbiology of a site when it means the microbes found there. The discipline name stands for its object, a familiar kind of metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 专业简称会说某部位的「微生物学」，实际指的是该处检出的微生物；学科名代替了它的研究对象，这是常见的转喻。

intro.en: Microbiology was coined in English in 1880 by joining the Greek prefix micro- to biology, a word itself only sixty years older. Its history shows how a new instrument, the microscope, created a new science.
intro.cn: microbiology 于 1880 年在英语中由希腊前缀 micro- 与 biology 组合而成，而 biology 本身只比它早六十年。它的历史显示，一件新工具——显微镜——如何创造出一门新科学。

items.en: Greek mikros, Attic smikros, meant 'small'. The Latinized prefix micro- entered scientific English as the standard marker of the very small. Beekes suspects a Pre-Greek origin, so the deeper etymology is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 mikros（阿提卡形式 smikros）意为「小」；拉丁化前缀 micro- 作为「极小」的标准标记进入科学英语。Beekes 怀疑它源自前希腊语底层，因此更深词源不确定。

items.en: Biology was suggested in 1802 by Treviranus and introduced in French by Lamarck, entering English by 1819. It joins Greek bios 'life' and -logia 'study, discourse'.
items.cn: biology 由特雷维拉努斯于 1802 年提出，并由拉马克以法语引入，1819 年进入英语；它由希腊 bios「生命」与 -logia「研究、论述」构成。

items.en: Greek -logia came from -log-, the combining form of legein 'to speak, tell', itself from a root meaning 'to gather, pick out'. Hence -logy names a disciplined way of speaking about a subject.
items.cn: 希腊 -logia 来自 -log-，即 legein「说、讲述」的组合形式，其词根意为「收集、拣选」；因此 -logy 命名的是关于某主题的一套有纪律的论述方式。

items.en: Microbiology is recorded from 1880, coined in English from micro- and biology. The same period produced microbiologist (1882) and the adjective microbiological.
items.cn: microbiology 记录于 1880 年，在英语中由 micro- 与 biology 构成；同一时期还产生了 microbiologist（1882）与形容词 microbiological。

items.en: Pasteur's and Koch's work in the 1870s and 1880s gave the new science its first great successes: sterilisation, pure culture and the identification of specific pathogens.
items.cn: 巴斯德与科赫在十九世纪七十至八十年代的工作，给这门新科学带来最初的重大成功：灭菌、纯培养与特定病原的鉴定。

items.en: The older name bacteriology covered only bacteria. Microbiology became the wider term once protists, fungi and later viruses were studied with the same methods. The shift is a widening of the object, not a change of root.
items.cn: 较早的 bacteriology 只涵盖细菌；当原生生物、真菌以及后来的病毒用同样方法研究之后，microbiology 成为更宽的名称。这一变化是研究对象的扩展，而不是词根的更换。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same stem that occupy other grammatical or professional slots. The second group holds neighbouring disciplines, each with a narrower object.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干上占据其他语法或职业位置的词；第二组是相邻学科，各自的研究对象更窄。

entries.definition: A person who practises microbiology. The ending -ist marks the practitioner, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 从事微生物学的人；词尾 -ist 标记从业者，而不是学科。

entries.definition: Relating to microbiology or its methods, as in microbiological safety. It describes the discipline's procedures rather than the organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 与微生物学或其方法有关的，如微生物学安全；描述的是学科程序，而不是生物体。

entries.definition: Of microbes themselves. It is the object-level adjective, while microbiological is the discipline-level one.
entries.definitionCN: 指微生物本身的形容词；它是对象层面的形容词，而 microbiological 是学科层面的。

entries.definition: The study of bacteria only. It is a subset of microbiology and was the older name for much of the same work.
entries.definitionCN: 只研究细菌的学科；它是微生物学的子集，也曾是大部分同类工作的旧名称。

entries.definition: The study of viruses, which are not cells and are often excluded from microorganisms. It is a separate discipline with separate methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究病毒的学科；病毒不是细胞，常被排除在微生物之外，因此它是一门有独立方法的独立学科。

entries.definition: The study of fungi, including yeasts and moulds. Many fungi are microorganisms, but the discipline is defined by the group, not the size.
entries.definitionCN: 研究真菌（包括酵母与霉菌）的学科；许多真菌是微生物，但这门学科按类群而非大小定义。

entries.definition: The industrial use of living systems, microbes among them. It is an application of microbiology rather than a branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 对生命系统（包括微生物）的工业利用；它是微生物学的应用，而不是其分支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: micro- 'small' + biology 'study of life' + -logy 'science of': the science of small life.
normal.cn: micro-「小」+ biology「生命研究」+ -logy「……学」：研究微小生命的科学。

normal.en: The word was coined in 1880, one year after microbial and two after microbe.
normal.cn: 这个词于 1880 年创制，比 microbial 晚一年，比 microbe 晚两年。

normal.en: The family runs microbiology, microbiologist, microbiological, microbiologically, microbe, microbial and microbiome.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 microbiology、microbiologist、microbiological、microbiologically、microbe、microbial、microbiome。

normal.en: Prefixes mark the branch: clinical, food, environmental, molecular and industrial microbiology.
normal.cn: 限定语标出分支：临床、食品、环境、分子与工业微生物学。

normal.en: Microbiology is wider than bacteriology because its object is defined by size, not by kingdom.
normal.cn: microbiology 比 bacteriology 宽，因为它的对象按大小定义，而不是按生物界定义。

abstract.en: Picture a science that began the day a lens made a hidden world visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一门科学，始于镜片让隐藏世界变得可见的那一天。

abstract.en: Picture a department where every shelf holds a dish of invisible citizens.
abstract.cn: 想象一个院系，每个架子上都放着一盘看不见的居民。

abstract.en: Picture a single cell asked to explain both a disease and a loaf of bread.
abstract.cn: 想象要求一个细胞同时解释一场疾病和一条面包。

examples.en: Microbiology turned the unknown outbreak into a named species.
examples.cn: 微生物学把不明疫情变成了一个有名字的物种。

examples.en: She studied microbiology before moving into public health.
examples.cn: 她在转入公共卫生之前学习过微生物学。

examples.en: Industrial microbiology keeps the fermentation tanks free of spoilage.
examples.cn: 工业微生物学让发酵罐免于腐败。

dict_mnemonic.text: micro-（微小）+ biology（生物学）→ 研究微小生物的学科 → microbiology 微生物学

root: 希腊 mikros「小」→ 拉丁化 micro-；希腊 bios「生命」+ -logia「研究、论述」→ biology（1819 年入英语）→ 1880 年英语合成 micro- + biology = microbiology。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the science itself to its institutional, clinical, industrial, environmental, practical, teaching and metonymic uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从这门科学本身，走向它的建制、临床、工业、环境、实践、教学与转喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of labelled dishes on a bench, a microscope and a report being filled in.
core.cn: 核心意象：实验台上一排贴标签的培养皿、显微镜，以及正在填写的报告。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: the organised study of small life is the root sense from which the others radiate.
branches.cn: 知识：关于微小生命的系统研究是根义，其他义项都由它辐射而出。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND TEACHING: a science can be a department or a course, because people organise and teach it.
branches.cn: 建制与教学：一门科学可以是一个院系或一门课，因为人们会组织它、教授它。

branches.en: APPLIED SETTINGS: the clinic names pathogens, the factory manages cultures.
branches.cn: 应用场景：诊所命名病原，工厂管理菌种。

branches.en: ENVIRONMENT: the same methods move outdoors to soil, water and air.
branches.cn: 环境：同样的方法移到户外，用于土壤、水体与空气。

branches.en: HANDS AND OBJECT: techniques are the hands of the science, and 'the microbiology of a site' is its object standing in for it.
branches.cn: 双手与对象：技术是这门科学的双手，而「某处的微生物学」是它的研究对象代它出场。

intro.en: Microbiology stacks three Greek elements: a prefix of smallness, a root of life, and a suffix of disciplined study.
intro.cn: microbiology 叠合了三个希腊成分：表示「微小」的前缀、表示「生命」的词根，以及表示「系统研究」的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The elements reached English through Latinized scientific forms: micro- from Greek mikros, biology from New Latin biologia, and -logy from Latin -logia. No single classical Latin word lies behind the compound.
latinIntro.cn: 这些成分经拉丁化的科学形式进入英语：micro- 来自希腊 mikros，biology 来自新拉丁 biologia，-logy 来自拉丁 -logia。这个复合词背后并没有单一的古典拉丁词。

items.exampleCN: 微生物学有自己的方法。

items.meaningCN: 从事这门科学的从业者
items.exampleCN: 微生物学家判读了培养皿。

items.meaning: from a microbiological point of view
items.exampleCN: 该样本在微生物学上是洁净的。

items.example: The microbe was cultured in agar.
items.exampleCN: 这种微生物在琼脂中培养。

items.example: The microbiome project sampled many sites.
items.exampleCN: 微生物组计划在许多地点取样。

definition_zh: 微观经济学；研究单个消费者、厂商与单个市场如何作出选择的经济学分支
definition_en: the branch of economics that studies how individual consumers, firms and single markets make choices and set prices
core_image: 一枚放大镜移到一个菜市场摊位上，画面里只剩一个买主和一个卖主在讨价还价
scene: 菜市场里其余摊位都被略去，只留下一张桌子、一个买主和一个卖主，研究者记录他们如何议价。Microeconomics explains how a single firm decides what price to charge when its rivals are watching.
sceneCN: 菜市场其余摊位被略去，只留一张桌子、一个买主与一个卖主，研究者记录议价过程；句中的 microeconomics 指「研究单个消费者、厂商与市场的分支」（第 1 个义项：以个体经济单位为研究对象的经济学分支）。图中可辨识物件：放大镜、菜摊、价签、记账本。

pos.zh: 微观经济学；个体经济学

derivatives.zh: 微观经济的；个体经济的
微观经济学家
微观计量经济学
微观计量经济学的

senses.title: The branch studying single units
senses.titleCN: 研究个体经济单位的学科分支
senses.definition: the division of economics that studies individual consumers, firms and markets rather than national totals
senses.definitionCN: 研究单个消费者、厂商与市场而非国民总量的经济学分支
senses.example: Microeconomics begins with one household buying bread.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济学从一个购买面包的家庭开始。
senses.why: The prefix marks small scale and the base names the discipline, so the compound means the study of the economy at the level of single units.
senses.whyCN: 前缀标记小尺度，基础词指学科，因此这个复合词意为「在单个单位层面研究经济」。

senses.title: The university subject
senses.definition: the name of a standard first course and textbook in economics degrees
senses.definitionCN: 经济学学位中一门标准入门课程与教材的名称
senses.example: Microeconomics is usually the first economics course students meet.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济学通常是学生接触的第一门经济学课程。
senses.why: When a branch is taught in a fixed sequence, its name becomes a subject title, and this branch is conventionally the introductory one.
senses.whyCN: 当分支按固定顺序讲授，其名称便成为科目名，而这个分支传统上正是入门的那一门。

senses.title: Price formation and equilibrium
senses.definition: the analysis of how supply and demand set a price in a single market
senses.definitionCN: 分析单个市场中供给与需求如何决定价格
senses.example: Microeconomics shows how a shortage pushes the price of a single good up.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济学说明短缺如何推高单一商品的价格。
senses.why: Because the small-scale unit is a single market, the branch's oldest task is to explain the price formed there.
senses.whyCN: 由于小尺度的单位是单个市场，这个分支最古老的任务就是解释在那里形成的价格。

senses.title: Consumer choice and utility
senses.definition: the study of how one person weighs wants, income and prices before buying
senses.definitionCN: 研究个人在购买前如何权衡欲望、收入与价格
senses.example: Microeconomics models the consumer as choosing between two goods on a fixed budget.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济学把消费者建模为在固定预算下于两种商品之间作选择。
senses.why: If the unit of analysis is one person, the natural question is what that person chooses and why, which the branch formalises as utility.
senses.whyCN: 若分析单位是一个人，自然的问题就是这个人选择什么、为何选择，该分支把它形式化为效用。

senses.title: Firm production and cost
senses.titleCN: 厂商的生产与成本决策
senses.definition: the study of how one business combines inputs and decides output and price
senses.definitionCN: 研究单个企业如何组合投入并决定产量与价格
senses.example: Microeconomics asks how a bakery decides whether to hire a second baker.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济学追问一家面包店如何决定是否再雇一名面包师。
senses.why: The same individual-level lens applied to a producer turns into questions of input, cost and output.
senses.whyCN: 同一套个体层面的视角用在生产者身上，就转为投入、成本与产量的问题。

senses.title: Market structure and competition
senses.definition: the comparison of monopoly, oligopoly and competitive markets by the number and power of sellers
senses.definitionCN: 按卖者数量与势力比较垄断、寡头与竞争性市场
senses.example: Microeconomics predicts that a monopoly will charge more than a competitive market.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济学预测垄断者会比竞争性市场要价更高。
senses.why: Once single markets are the unit, they can be classified by how many sellers meet how many buyers, and the branch compares those structures.
senses.whyCN: 一旦以单个市场为单位，就可以按卖者与买者的数量给市场分类，该分支便比较这些结构。

senses.title: Applied microeconomic policy
senses.definition: the use of individual-level analysis to judge taxes, regulation, labour and public programmes
senses.definitionCN: 用个体层面分析评判税收、监管、劳动与公共项目
senses.example: Applied microeconomics evaluated whether the childcare subsidy raised employment.
senses.exampleCN: 应用微观经济学评估育儿补贴是否提高了就业。
senses.why: Policy questions about specific groups and prices fall inside the small-scale lens, so the branch supplies the evaluation tools.
senses.whyCN: 关于特定群体与价格的政策问题落在小尺度视角之内，该分支便提供评估工具。

senses.title: Microfoundations for the whole
senses.titleCN: 为总体解释提供微观基础
senses.definition: the methodological role of explaining aggregate outcomes through the choices of individual agents
senses.definitionCN: 以个体行为者的选择来解释总体结果的方法论角色
senses.example: Microeconomics supplies the microfoundations that aggregate models are built on.
senses.exampleCN: 微观经济学提供总体模型赖以建立的微观基础。
senses.why: Even when the question is national, the small-scale branch can claim authority by showing that totals are the sum of individual decisions.
senses.whyCN: 即使问题是全国的，小尺度分支也能通过说明总量是个体决策之和来主张自己的解释力。

intro.en: Microeconomics joins a Greek prefix meaning 'small' to economics, which descends from Greek oikonomia through Latin oeconomia. The compound and its adjective are generally thought to have settled around the 1940s as the discipline divided into small-scale and large-scale branches; the exact first year is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词把一个表示「小的」的希腊前缀加在经济学科之名上，而后者经拉丁 oeconomia 源自希腊 oikonomia。一般认为这个复合词及其形容词形式在二十世纪四十年代前后随学科分工固定下来；具体首见年份来源不确定。

items.en: Mikros meant 'small, little, slight' and formed the opposite in scale to the large prefix used for the whole economy.
items.cn: mikros 意为「小的、微小的、轻微的」，在尺度上与表示整体经济的大前缀相对。

items.en: Oikonomia, from oikos 'household' and nemein 'to manage', named the running of a household and later of public affairs.
items.cn: oikonomia 由 oikos「家宅」与 nemein「管理」构成，先指经营家宅，后也指管理公共事务。

items.en: Latin oeconomia carried the word into European learned usage, covering the management of an estate or a state.
items.cn: 拉丁 oeconomia 把这个词带入欧洲学术用语，其范围包括庄园或国家的管理。

items.en: In the nineteenth century political economy was shortened to economics, giving the base to which the small-scale prefix was later attached.
items.cn: 十九世纪政治经济学缩称为经济学，为后来加接小尺度前缀提供了基础词。

items.en: The adjective is generally thought to have appeared in the early twentieth century, when analysis of single units needed a name of its own.
items.cn: 一般认为这个形容词在二十世纪初出现，当时针对单个单位的分析需要一个自己的名称。

items.en: The noun is generally thought to have settled around the 1940s as teaching and research split into individual-level and whole-economy branches; the exact year is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个名词在二十世纪四十年代前后固定，当时教学与研究分成个体层面与整体经济两个分支；具体年份不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds forms from the same compound that differ in word class or scale; the near-meaning group holds smaller theories that each take one part of the individual-level picture.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一复合词中词性或尺度不同的形式；近义组收的是各自的更小理论，只取个体层面图景的一部分。

entries.definition: Describes individual-level analysis, as in microeconomic evidence; it cannot serve as the name of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 描述个体层面的分析，如微观经济证据；它不能用作课程名称。

entries.definition: Studies national totals; the two words share their ending and are routinely paired, so the prefixes are the only thing that keeps them apart.
entries.definitionCN: 研究国民总量；两词词尾相同且常被成对使用，真正区分它们的只有前缀。

entries.definition: The whole subject, of which the individual-level branch is one part; it is broader, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 整个学科，个体层面分支只是其中一部分；它范围更广，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A casual abbreviation for the branch or a word for anything small; it never appears in a formal course title.
entries.definitionCN: 对该分支的随口简称，也可泛指细小之物；它从不出现于正式课程名称。

entries.definition: An older name for the study of how prices form in single markets; it covers the price sense but not consumer choice in general.
entries.definitionCN: 研究单个市场价格如何形成的旧名；它覆盖价格方面，却不涵盖一般的消费者选择。

entries.definition: The part of the branch that models one buyer's preferences and budget; it is a component, not the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 该分支中为单个买主的偏好与预算建模的部分；它是组成部分，而非整个领域。

entries.definition: Studies how firms compete and how markets are structured; it is the branch's firm-centred wing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究企业如何竞争、市场如何构成；它是该分支以企业为中心的一翼。

entries.definition: Asks whether a market outcome is good for people overall; it evaluates results rather than explaining the choices behind them.
entries.definitionCN: 追问某一市场结果对人们整体是否有利；它评判结果，而不解释其背后的选择。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here use the real Greek small prefix, the real household root behind economics, and the real division of labour inside the modern discipline.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自表示「小」的真实希腊前缀、经济学背后真实的治家词根，以及现代学科内部真实的分工。

normal.en: Mikros means small, so the prefix marks the scale of one buyer, one firm, one market.
normal.cn: mikros 意为小，因此这个前缀标记的是一个买主、一家企业、一个市场的尺度。

normal.en: Oikonomia, household management, is the same root that gave economics.
normal.cn: oikonomia 即治家之术，正是给经济学提供词根的那个词。

normal.en: Price theory was the older label for this work before the compound became standard.
normal.cn: 在这个复合词通行之前，这项工作旧称价格理论。

normal.en: The pair with macroeconomics is built into the word: small scale against large scale.
normal.cn: 它与宏观经济学的配对就写在这个词里：小尺度对大尺度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the teaching sense: principles of microeconomics, applied microeconomics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出教学义：微观经济学原理、应用微观经济学。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass held over one stall while every other stall is blurred out.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚放大镜停在某一个摊位上，其余摊位都被虚化。

abstract.en: Picture one buyer and one seller at a table, with a researcher writing down every word they trade.
abstract.cn: 想象桌边只有一个买主和一个卖主，研究者在旁记下他们交换的每一句话。

abstract.en: Picture a single price tag that can be moved by one decision rather than by a national trend.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签，推动它的不是全国趋势，而是某一个决定。

examples.en: Microeconomics teaches students to treat a household and a firm as the basic units of analysis.
examples.cn: 微观经济学教学生把家庭与企业当作分析的基本单位。

examples.en: The regulator used microeconomics to argue that two merging shops would raise local prices.
examples.cn: 监管者用微观经济学论证两家商店合并会推高本地价格。

examples.en: Without microeconomics, the aggregate model would have no account of individual choices at all.
examples.cn: 若没有微观经济学，总体模型便完全无法交代个体选择。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「麦克柔伊科诺米克斯」：麦克柔先生只盯着一个摊位的一买一卖，算的是小处的账。

root: 希腊 mikros「小的」+ 希腊 oikonomia（oikos「家宅」+ nemein「管理」）→ 拉丁 oeconomia → 英语中的经济学；再加表示「小」的前缀构成微观经济学，一般认为二十世纪四十年代前后随学科分工定型，首见年份来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: the branch is named and taught, then narrowed to price, to the buyer, to the firm and to market structure, applied to policy, and finally offered as the individual-level foundation beneath aggregate claims.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：先给分支命名并进入课堂，再收窄到价格、买主、企业、市场结构，继而用于政策，最后成为支撑总体结论的个体层面基础。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one stall under a magnifying glass, where a single bargain holds the whole picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：放大镜下的一处摊位，一桩买卖便构成整幅图景。

branches.en: NAMING AND TEACHING: the branch takes the single unit as its object and becomes the standard first course.
branches.cn: 命名与教学：该分支以单个单位为对象，并成为标准的入门课程。

branches.en: PRICE AND BUYER: supply meets demand at one price, and one person chooses under a fixed budget.
branches.cn: 价格与买主：供需在一个价格上相遇，而个人在固定预算下作选择。

branches.en: FIRM AND MARKET: one producer weighs cost and output, and markets are sorted by the number of sellers.
branches.cn: 企业与市场：单个生产者权衡成本与产量，市场则按卖者数目分类。

branches.en: APPLIED POLICY: individual-level evidence is used to judge taxes, subsidies and regulation.
branches.cn: 应用政策：用个体层面的证据评判税收、补贴与监管。

branches.en: FOUNDATION: individual choices are offered as the base on which national totals rest.
branches.cn: 基础：个体选择被当作国民总量所依托的底层。

intro.en: The word is a scale prefix plus a discipline noun: a Greek element of smallness in front, and the household-derived name of economics behind.
intro.cn: 这个词是「尺度前缀加学科名词」：前面是表示细小的希腊成分，后面是由治家一词演变来的经济学之名。

latinIntro.en: Latin oeconomia and oeconomicus provide the older European forms of the economics half, while the smallness element was latinised as a combining form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 oeconomia 与 oeconomicus 提供「经济学」那一半较早的欧洲形式，而表示细小的成分则被拉丁化为组合形式。

items.structure: prefix of Greek origin meaning small
items.meaning: at a small scale, one unit at a time
items.example: The prefix fixes the unit of study at one buyer or one firm.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把研究单位锁定为一个买主或一家企业。

items.example: Mikros supplied the smallness element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: mikros 提供了这个复合词中表示细小的成分。

items.structure: Greek compound noun, oikos plus nemein
items.example: Oikonomia is the oldest layer of the base word.
items.exampleCN: oikonomia 是基础词最古老的一层。

items.meaning: management of an estate or state
items.example: Oeconomia carried the idea into learned Latin.
items.exampleCN: oeconomia 把这个观念带入学术拉丁语。

items.meaning: the study of production, trade and resources
items.meaningCN: 研究生产、贸易与资源的学科
items.example: Economics is the base to which the smallness prefix is added.
items.exampleCN: 经济学是加接细小前缀的基础词。

items.structure: suffix naming a field of study
items.example: The suffix makes a subject name out of a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成学科名称。

items.meaning: relating to individual buyers, firms and markets
items.meaningCN: 与单个买主、企业与市场相关的
items.example: Microeconomic evidence comes from household surveys.
items.exampleCN: 微观经济证据来自家庭调查。

items.meaning: a specialist in the individual-level branch
items.example: A microeconomist studies one market at a time.
items.exampleCN: 微观经济学家一次研究一个市场。

items.structure: prefix of Greek origin meaning large
items.meaning: at a large scale, taken as a whole
items.example: The opposite prefix names the whole-economy branch.
items.exampleCN: 相对的前缀命名整体经济分支。

items.meaning: the discipline of single units and single markets
items.meaningCN: 研究单个单位与单个市场的学科
items.example: Microeconomics became the standard first course.
items.exampleCN: 微观经济学成为标准的入门课程。
